reviews.author: Kim M.
reviews.text: We had no problem getting a site even on a holiday weekend.  Just have to get here early.

reviews.author: Thu Ha  Thi N.
reviews.text: C3 was good spot, next to restroom. Quiet and shady spot

reviews.author: Joseph H.
reviews.text: The email i received from the campground a couple days before my trip said "buy it where you burn it" regarding firewood. So we bought a bunch of firewood, because that's my favorite part of campingand we had limited camp stove fuel. However, when we arrived at the campsite, there were "burn ban" flyers all over the campground that were clearly weeks old. It was extremely frustrating and disappointing. Plus, no soap in the bathrooms.

reviews.author: Timothy W.
reviews.text: Campground was quiet and relaxing, in spite of the hundreds of visitors going up the main road just outside.

reviews.author: Kent B.
reviews.text: I arrived around 12-1 pm.  Trying to get a FF site.  I got the last one availble that might fit my trailer.  The ranger at the campground station was helpful and let me get set up in it. before locking it in.  Campground was ell maintained.

reviews.author: Kasun D.
reviews.text: Very calm and pleasant campsite closer to everything

reviews.author: Kasun D.
reviews.text: Excellent choice if you like to stay closer to Pradise area. Overall well maintained camp ground. But need to add few more restrooms specially to Loop B

reviews.author: Frank S.
reviews.text:
Some sites are not nice, in part because trees have been cut.  Too many trees have been cut down, and also left as unsightly stumps.  Other sites are OK.  

Also people made noise during quite hours, including a guy idling his truck next to us starting at 7:30 AM and music playing at 9:30 pm.  

Showers would also be a big plus.

reviews.author: Rylee W.
reviews.text: Very beautiful campground, I drive a Jeep Wrangler JL and the parking space was perfect, I did have to back in as it was at an angle though (keep that in mind). The tent space is down about 11 stairs, but the picnic table was at the top next to the parking area which was nice! Not super private to the front and side, but everyone was quiet and I had no problems with feeling like I was being eavesdropped on! Bathrooms were very close and very clean!

reviews.author: Tim E.
reviews.text: Across the street from the Wonderland trail and full of beautiful big trees Cougar Camp is a well situated camp. Close to Paradise and Longmire it has quick access to many natural attractions

reviews.author: Fallon H.
reviews.text: Loved this campground!

reviews.author: Karen A.
reviews.text: Most sites are spacious, the only request would be to have a separate loop that did not allow campfires for those of us with lung disease. Very hard to breathe in a beautiful forest.

reviews.author: Caroline  T.
reviews.text: Gorgeous campsite, kind rangers, great time.

reviews.author: Elizabeth W.
reviews.text: Great campground and site

reviews.author: Erika  Z.
reviews.text:
Great campsite for our two man tent and car. About equal distance to two restrooms, just a little walk away if that is something you’re worried about. 
Great campsite, would recommend!

reviews.author: Emily  L.
reviews.text: Walkable to some trails and close to Longmire are and visitor center. Only 25 min from Paradise. No showers, bathrooms were fine.

reviews.author: Christine  G.
reviews.text: Great campground near Paradise visitor center at Mount Rainier. Some campsites require a reservation, and others are first come first serve.

reviews.author: Cynthia A.
reviews.text: Beautiful location! Loved our experience here!

reviews.author: Maranda  B.
reviews.text: Got a FCFS camping spot! Convenient location.

reviews.author: Kristin H.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our 1 night here. We wish that advance reservations would have been possible for our first night that we had to find last minute accommodations for since it was only ffs on Father's day weekend.

reviews.author: Dominick O.
reviews.text: Wonderful campground with easy access to the park. For the RV crowd: 22’ travel trailer with 16’ vehicle and plenty of sites that would accommodate. Wouldn’t recommend much larger though due to some tight turns on campground road.

reviews.author: Jesse A.
reviews.text: Campsite is on a busy road with no privacy

reviews.author: Michael  H.
reviews.text: We went in the shoulder season just before it gets busy.  It was still first come first serve.  People were running through occupied sites and looking around ones that were scheduled to vacate in the mornings.  I don't recommend a trailer, cause all the Tundras, Sprinter vans, and subaru's, rush to the larger pull through RV Spots.  There were multiple sites available when we had our turn, but only one available for our trailer.  We got lucky.  IF you get in, there are numerous hikes and waterfalls, for all ages and abilities to get to.  As always the National Park Rangers were all extremely friendly and helpful.  With the crowds, came the inconsiderate people blazing trails through protected meadows.  The NP Law had their hands full.   Very beautiful and a great family experience.

reviews.author: Konrad G.
reviews.text: Ein sehr schöner Platz. Gut organisiert

reviews.author: Tim C.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our stay.

reviews.author: Jess H.
reviews.text: This site has people sitting there for hours everyday selling firewood. It’s pretty awkward.

reviews.author: marie m.
reviews.text: Nice campground with shade and mostly large sites. Some sites are even pull through.  Nice walk to the waterfall from the campground. There is a water fountain outside the toilets which was nice but no other water sources. I would have liked some hot water in the bathroom and some ability to dry your hands. Bring $15 for a small bundle of wood.

reviews.author: Janis J.
reviews.text: The campground is showing some wear and tear, but it's in a beautiful and handy location.  We appreciated all the pull-through sites.  The restrooms are nice with flush toilets and sinks.  However Loop B doesn't have a restroom.  You have to walk to Loops A or C.  Work is being done to remove fallen trees.

reviews.author: Fred C.
reviews.text: Beautiful campgrounds. Wonderful sights, stellar smells, friendly people. There was no dump station, however

reviews.author: Gale M.
reviews.text: Pretty campsites accessible to multiple hiking. trails. No water available to fill tanks. Drinking water available at restrooms. Paradise area gets very busy. Get there early to secure parking. Restrooms in the park were the dirtiest I’ve seen in 3 months of travels.

reviews.author: steve h.
reviews.text: Great location. Nice tent site. Bathrooms not the cleanest, but certainly acceptable.

reviews.author: Kee-Hoon P.
reviews.text: Well prepared and well service camping lot.  Thank you for your service.  Well used tax money.

reviews.author: Russ S.
reviews.text: Refreshing to be in a national park campground where all the staff are helpful and accommodating!

reviews.author: Robert T.
reviews.text: Lots of nice campsites to choose from.  The campground is clean and orderly.  The Ranger Program on Saturday night was excellent.  A number of enjoyable hikes you can start from this area.

reviews.author: Marc F.
reviews.text: Very quiet and peaceful camp ground.

reviews.author: Guy W.
reviews.text: Rangers are always very nice and helpful. Campground is well run. Restrooms are clean.

reviews.author: Dana K.
reviews.text: Great time

reviews.author: Wade T.
reviews.text: The rangers at the campground office were great! Helpful and actually there to answer questions. They pointed us in the right direction for hiking and gave us a map with helpful information, and not just the park brochure. They were the ones that really made the experience smooth.

reviews.author: Deborah W.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground.

reviews.author: JAY T.
reviews.text: Beautiful setting. Nicely spaced campsites. Level tent site. I enjoyed the 2 days I spent at Cougar Rock campground.

reviews.author: Crit C.
reviews.text: A pretty nice campground with lots of options for site size.  For sleeping in a vehicle or camper, the flattest sites were a bit more limited, but still a good amount to choose from. The bathrooms would be my biggest complaint, they had TP but thats it.  No paper towels or hand dryers and no soap.  A lovely setting walking distance from trails and a quick drive to lots of other things in the park.

reviews.author: Michael E.
reviews.text: Happy there wasn’t a burn ban. The staff there is always so friendly.

reviews.author: Liv M.
reviews.text: The system for choosing a site worked well for us--to drive around and choose 3 and return to the office. We got our first choice. It was lovely and the site was very flat for our van.

reviews.author: Emma K.
reviews.text: This campsite was clean, quiet enough for being so full, and more private than I was expecting given how small it is. The site was large enough that we weren’t on top of our neighbors and we felt comfortable and safe as two young women. The bathrooms were unfortunately right down the hill past one other campsite but with no trail we didn’t want to just cut through their site. This meant walking quite a distance to get around the loop, but the restrooms were large and clean. If you’re headed to paradise on your trip, this is the perfect place to stay. And however early you think you should get to paradise in the morning, leave earlier. It was the most overflowed parking situation we experienced on our trip that august to more than ten national parks.

reviews.author: Olga A.
reviews.text: Big sites, a lot of trees between them. Clean washrooms. Be aware that there is no warm water and soap there. Nevertheless I would be happy to return to this campground again. Closeness to everything that Mt Rainer can offer is unbeatable.

reviews.author: Pamela D.
reviews.text:
This is a nice campground. Very large, but spread out enough. Some campsites are fabulous - others not so good. Bathrooms are adequate, not super clean but the toilets work and water is available. 
RV DUMP has been out of order for years.

reviews.author: Linnaea  S.
reviews.text: Good bathrooms for a campground.

reviews.author: Linnaea  S.
reviews.text:
Good bathrooms for a campsite.
Campsites are arranged to give maximum privacy in close proximity.

reviews.author: Linnaea  S.
reviews.text: Difficult to reserve campsites. Difficult to reserve more than one campsite together. No internet service which is required to obtain passes to Sunrise and Paradise. The campsite itself has a lot of slash. The campfire program was geared more towards children and didn't have as much information as I would have liked as an adult. Bathroom facilities good for a campground. Campsites are arranged to be relatively private given their closeness to each other.

reviews.author: Lynn S.
reviews.text: The campground was great. Spacious sites, seemed quiet even though it was fairly full. The showers were clean (and even had people cleaning them at 9 at night!). We would stay again.

reviews.author: Natalie L.
reviews.text: Loved this campground and its proximity to the skyline trail! We enjoyed our stay. Enjoyed walking to the bathroom area and seeing Mount Rainer on the way

reviews.author: Alaina W.
reviews.text: Great in park location, easy access facilities, nice flat tent space

reviews.author: Connor M.
reviews.text: Fantastic Stay! Campground was clean, not too crowded, and bathroom was a reasonable distance away from every campsite.

reviews.author: Scott R.
reviews.text:
My experience in the park was great.  However, it was very frustrating trying to get a camping spot on-line.  The website make you feel like the spots are all taken.  When I finally got a spot and was in there I found so many of the spots were not filled.  
People reserve them and don't show up.  I wish there was a confirmation process a week or so out to open up these spots to people who want them and are in the park.  Daily I saw people turned away from vacant spots.  Its a sad way to operate a popular spot.

reviews.author: Roger T.
reviews.text: N/A

reviews.author: Thriven Kumar Y.
reviews.text:
Campgroud is very nice with good restrooms, camping spots and starry sky views at night. It is very close to Mount Rainier trails.
Campfire was banned in the state during the time I visited but it is not mentioned in the campground website.

reviews.author: Joram D.
reviews.text:
Lovely spots, big enough for camper vans. Very attentive employees, they think ahead and think along.
We had a wonderful experience in Mount Rainier National Park.

reviews.author: John L.
reviews.text: We found an excellent spot to camp which was private and relaxing.

reviews.author: David S.
reviews.text: We had a wonderful visit. Peaceful.

reviews.author: Tery A.
reviews.text: Great camp ground to visit Rainer National Park from

reviews.author: Timothy F.
reviews.text: Cougar is a good location. The facility was clean. However, the site’s are small and mine was not level.

reviews.author: Marcie L.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite, only 40 minutes away from Crater lake! Will definitely stay there again.

reviews.author: Joy T.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with close access to Paradise area.

reviews.author: Brandon A.
reviews.text: Park rangers were great source of info on trails!

reviews.author: James G.
reviews.text: The campground was maintained well. Sites were large. Even though most sites were taken, it was quiet. The hosts were friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: Ting W.
reviews.text: This is a great campground! The location is very convenient for accessing trails. It’s perfect for anyone who enjoys hiking and exploring nature. The sites are well maintained, and the atmosphere is peaceful. I’d definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a relaxing outdoor getaway.

reviews.author: Alexandra F.
reviews.text: Beautiful Campground, close to Paradise, very friendly Ranger!

reviews.author: Karen G.
reviews.text: Great campground for a base from which to access fine hiking.

reviews.author: Min Y.
reviews.text: Upside:  many private campsites and super clean bathroom.  Downside: hilly campground and too few bathrooms.

reviews.author: Alyssa P.
reviews.text: Beautiful site.

reviews.author: Joseph T.
reviews.text: W

reviews.author: John R.
reviews.text: Highly recommended for proximity to visitor center and hikes.

reviews.author: Reese L.
reviews.text: The staff was very friendly and helped us pick out a great site. Very private sites and close to a lot in the park. Several people showed up to the advertised ranger talk, but it must have been canceled because a ranger did not show up. No soap in the bathrooms, but they were clean.

reviews.author: Garrett H.
reviews.text:
The restroom was cleanish, but it felt old and as if it only gets cleaned once a week whether it needs it or not. The campground was perfect for our little dome tent and the trees were close enough to rig up a fly for us to cook under...because it rained on us the entire time. We didn't mind, we were mostly dry all night.

It was first come, first served for spots since we camped at the beginning of October.

Highly recommend Cougar Rock when it was after school started back...can't speak to it during peak season.

reviews.author: Vicky H.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground!

reviews.author: Michael H.
reviews.text: Very scenic campground. Arrived on a Sunday and there were lots of first come first served sites available.

reviews.author: Vinca S.
reviews.text: Great campground! Was grateful for the first come, first serve protocol in the fall. Josh and the rest of the camp managers were very helpful and friendly, and made our stay a pleasure. Everyone was super considerate and friendly, except for that one couple with the fussy, loud child at 12am, but, hey, can't win them all, so bring ear plugs!

reviews.author: Laura B.
reviews.text: Great campsites. Clean and quiet. There were no gender neutral restrooms which would have been nice.

reviews.author: Michael R.
reviews.text: I’ve never had a bad camping experience but our neighbors absolutely destroyed this trip for us. They decided to park in our campsite which at first isn’t a big deal I thought it was weird they waited until we walked to the bathroom to make the move. It’s that they were in and out of their car opening and closing every door multiple times like they were making sure they still worked. Then they’d start the car opening and close the doors some more and then drive away. The first time was a bit annoying mostly confusing but it’s happened several more times all after quite hours and every time they’d shine their headlights directly at our tent and wake us up. After the third time I tried to confront them but they sped away in their car when they saw me approaching. The facilities themselves were great bathrooms clean garbage picked up I wish there was a way to get one of the rangers involved with ridiculous behaviors like this late at night.

reviews.author: Tiggy S.
reviews.text: Wonderful campsite

reviews.author: Siddharth G.
reviews.text: Excellent campground, top support from rangers and team. Would love to come back and camp/hike again here. :)

reviews.author: David C.
reviews.text: The Rangers were super friendly and helpful.  The campground and facilities were great.  It was nice to have so many hiking trails to take right out of the campground plus the short drive to Paradise to hike the trails up there.

reviews.author: Dale L.
reviews.text: Beautiful area, well maintained, convenient to trails.

reviews.author: MELISSA K.
reviews.text: The campground is nice, facilities are adequate and its in a great location.  the sites are a bit close together here but I didnt mind. We car camped for one night and had no issues.

reviews.author: Eric M.
reviews.text: Took one or two different hikes/walks every day. It was great.

reviews.author: Paula L.
reviews.text: Beautiful area.    Water available at common spigot and bathrooms were good.     Campsite was small but sufficed as we didn’t spend much time there during the day.    Campground was only partially open due to time of year.  Campground location was convenient

reviews.author: Mark W.
reviews.text: We were fortunate to get a first come/first serve spot in September. The ranger was nice and super helpful. And the campground is lovely - spaced out well, amazing trees, unique sites throughout. We'll be back!

reviews.author: Olaf S.
reviews.text: This is a very pleasant campground to stay at when you visit Mt. Rainier.  We are able to get a campsite in the shoulder season easier than in August.

reviews.author: Daisy Y.
reviews.text:
I was lucky to snag this spot in the late evening when it was on a first come, first served basis. The site is small, as the tent pad had enough space to fit my 2-person tent comfortably but that was it. Any larger of a tent could be an issue as there's this random log that's standing up-right on the site so that cuts off part of the available surface area.  Maybe if the 4-person tent faced the cars, then that could work to get in/out of the tent. In addition, there are about 3 steps up from the car area to the tent pad. The restrooms are close, but not super close as the closest one is in Loop C. Other than that, the spot was great!

The pictures make the driveway look big, but I would say it could fit a 4Runner from a length standpoint before parts of the car start sticking out into the road.

reviews.author: Curtis A.
reviews.text: Many, if not most, of the sites are not level. It was challenging to get our camper van reasonably level. And there is no WiFi coverage in the campground - you need to get near a visitor center to get coverage.

reviews.author: Chris A.
reviews.text: Cougar Rock campground is a cute campground in an awesome environment. However, sites were generally not level, no services, no dump or potable water fill. There is no cellular service in the area and because of the tree coverage, solar and Starlink are problematic. The campground does offer small bathrooms with flush toilets, utility sink, bottle fill station and bear safe food storage.

reviews.author: Niall C.
reviews.text: Excellent help from a Park Ranger.

reviews.author: Emily C.
reviews.text:
Campground was great.  Staff assigning sites were excellent and really knew their campground! 
Park is wonderful, lots of short, family friendly hikes

reviews.author: Carolyn W.
reviews.text: Great sites. Clean restrooms. Nice staff. Fantastic trails!

reviews.author: Tim J.
reviews.text: Not sure why 3 loops were closed but got the last site on a weekday in mid-September and we barely fit.

reviews.author: Nathan E.
reviews.text: I moved to this campsite after my first two nights due to the campground switching to first come first served and the closing of D and E loops for maintenance. The campsite was literally next to the bathroom which was convenient but the light from the bathroom was a tad bright. This site is also pretty close to the neighboring site so while I’d stay at Cougar Rock again, I’d probably not pick this particular site.

reviews.author: Nathan E.
reviews.text: I had a great stay at Cougar Rock and I’d definitely stay here again. I was at this site for my first two nights as it was the tail end of the reservation season and had to switch campsites for my last two nights. I liked how the tent area was elevated from the rest of the site. I’d definitely recommend this campground!  It’s about 10 minutes from Longmire and just a beautiful 30 minute drive from Paradise.

reviews.author: Laurie F.
reviews.text: Camped at a first come first serve site in mid-September for two nights. Easy reservation process with the Visitor Center the next day (we came in after hours). Limited sites open that time of year, but great to have several restrooms in each loop and nice, quiet sites while visiting the park.

reviews.author: Max M.
reviews.text: First time to camp at Cougar Rock.  I will be back.

reviews.author: Scott C.
reviews.text:
Great location within the park. Excellent campsites. Quiet at night. 
The Park Ranger at the campground station was very helpful, friendly, and informative.
I would only caution that site A24 has a very steep grade on the exit as a pull through. As a result, my sway bar bracket caught the pavement on the exit and broke off. This is why I rated at 4 stars, otherwise it would be a 5 star rating.

reviews.author: Steven H.
reviews.text: Campsite B25 was a good size and and had flat spots for 2 tents and was well spaced from the other campsites. Could hear the flow from the Nisqually River as we slept. Knocking 1 star bc there was no soap in men’s room.

reviews.author: Walter A.
reviews.text: We had a great site, but I was lucky to be able to drive around and pick the one I wanted.  Many are good for one tent but tough for two tents.  Lots of people sleep in vehicles these days it seems.  People who worked there were super nice.

reviews.author: Andy G.
reviews.text: Very clean really nice size camp sites and all campers and staff was super friendly.

reviews.author: Steve J.
reviews.text: Had spot 23 on the A loop. Was right up against an offshoot of the river. Had access to the main river which was nice, and cold! I would definitely recommend either loop B or C - more shade, trees and privacy. Bathrooms were clean but no showers. Trails were awesome.

reviews.author: John H.
reviews.text:
Positive: Our campsite had a view of Mt. Rainier (E025), which was nice.  The sites are nestled in the forest, so there is good shade provided by mature trees.  The campground is 20 minutes from Paradise.  When the office is open, the staff provides good advice and help.
Needs Improvement:  No dump station.  The closest was in Morton. We did not see a ranger or anyone to attend the campground.  So the sites were not cleaned up.  The burn ban seemed more like they did not want to have to clean up the fire pit. The bathroom closest to us had only a bottle fill station for water.  
NOTE: NO GENERATORS PERMITTED in loop E.

reviews.author: Austin B.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with excellent access to Rainier

reviews.author: Alan O.
reviews.text: Go across the street and take the trail up to Cramer Falls and/or hike down to Longmire for a snack and a walk around. Get up to Paradise early for better parking and better chance of seeing wildlife.

reviews.author: Leslie L.
reviews.text: Very enjoyable stay.

reviews.author: April M.
reviews.text: Policies concerning first come first serve site occupation need to be modified. Asking someone who is already occupying a site to move because they sold the site out from under you, to someone not there in person, ready to occupy the site, is unacceptable.

reviews.author: Cibin P.
reviews.text: Great facility. We went when it was quiet just before some sites started closing for winter. Staff were accomodating and helpful. Facility was clean and well maintained.

reviews.author: julie l.
reviews.text: Clean and quiet! Fairly large campground, some of the spots are shallow and less private, but overall a great experience. Very close to many attractions. Bear safe food boxes were present in our campsite

reviews.author: Sharon S.
reviews.text: I love this campground! You’re close to all the best parts of the Nisqually entrance side, you have bathrooms, and the price is right! The park staff are friendly and helpful!

reviews.author: Daeyou K.
reviews.text: Excellent

reviews.author: Andrew F.
reviews.text: Campsites are close together, but good proximity to paradise (20 min drive). Pretty average national Park campground. While my particular site was in the no generator loop, it is very close proximity to the R sites, which do allow generators and are quite loud.

reviews.author: Jay B.
reviews.text: Nice private campsite. Facilities in good condition

reviews.author: Diana K.
reviews.text: Road behind site is kinda noisy. Friend complained about it being too far from bathroom. Bathroom is very buggy at night and morning. Kitchen sink is broken. Tent area is suitable for one big tent or two small two persons ones.

reviews.author: HELEN Y.
reviews.text: We were so lucky to get a spot from a reservation cancellation on the day we made an impromptu trip to Mt. Rainier. The campsites were well maintained. 10 miniutes drive to the Paradise visitor center and multiple sightseeing spots, including Skyline trail, Myrtle Falls etc. Really a pleasant experience.

reviews.author: Lisa G.
reviews.text: Nice location and accessible off road site. Very close to Longmire and on the way to Paradise.

reviews.author: Roy H.
reviews.text: Nice campground, located in a good spot between Longmire and Paradise. Decent campsites, although a bit close to each other; we had some noisy neighbors one night, but overall very nice.

reviews.author: Stacey S.
reviews.text: I was able to grab a last minute reservation so I could car camp.while visiting the park. The campground was very clean, I had a  semi-private lot, it was quiet, the campground ranger was friendly amd helpful, and the views were awesome! I highly recommend this campground if you want to stay in the park for your time there.

reviews.author: Kip M.
reviews.text: We enjoyed seven August nights in beautiful weather at Cougar Rock Campground. The Stevens Canyon Road has been upgraded very nicely, with some paving and painting still ongoing on the west end. Our site was spacious and wooded. It was a short walk from the campground to cross the rushing Nisqually River on a log bridge leading to the Carter Falls Trail. We hiked 33 miles of the Wonderland Trail with Cougar Rock as our base camp. Views were great everywhere. Rangers were friendly and helpful, especially with hike planning and wilderness camping reservations.

reviews.author: Anthony A.
reviews.text: Due to budgets cuts the staff was very difficult to locate and get help from. There were very few rangers in the park which will eventually lead to lawlessness and a park in distress.

reviews.author: Valeriya S.
reviews.text: Wow, we were blown away by this site. It was fantastic and we’re from Vancouver Island so we’ve camped a bunch. Huge sites, incredibly clean, absolutely silent, trees provide privacy, clean facilities, toilets, changing table, and sinks. There was a water refilling area at the restroom and each site has its own bear cache. The check in and check out were easy. Pretty great start to a road trip!

reviews.author: Brennan M.
reviews.text: Horrible. No staff at desk, no fires allowed (even though people were having fires next to us), unclean bathrooms.

reviews.author: Torre N.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with lots of trees. Bathrooms are clean. Quiet. Close to several nice trails.

reviews.author: Jim F.
reviews.text: Very nice ranger at check-in. The amenities are very basic however as you might expect. The bathrooms, while clean, are desperately in need for a major upgrade. America has the best national parks, but we need to invest in the infrastructure and ongoing upkeep. The huckleberries are ripe and we did lots of bike riding in the campground loops - perfect for a 5 year old!!

reviews.author: Tammie S.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with basic amenities. We enjoyed the Ranger talk at the amphitheater.

reviews.author: Matthew C.
reviews.text: As expected.  Clean and quiet.  Staff is awesome.

reviews.author: Megan K.
reviews.text: The Campground was way more private than expected! Sites were spaced apart, staggered, and surrounded by trees. Plentiful and abundance access to potable water. The bathrooms were some of the nicest at a Campground. Quiet and clean. 100% reccomend.

reviews.author: John D.
reviews.text:
Great spot. Easy to get to the restroom and water. If the closest bathroom is full, go down a ways and find the 2nd one. It has 2 stalls instead of the 1

All in all, we had a good time. Its close to paradise and food at longmire

reviews.author: Seunggoo J.
reviews.text: The picnic table and tent site at E008 were separated, which was nice, but the site itself was a bit small. The restrooms were well maintained and very clean, and overall the campground was extremely quiet.

reviews.author: Chris S.
reviews.text:
The park rangers were some of the most friendly and helpful rangers that I’ve ever encountered. 
The campground was also very clean.

reviews.author: Ellen K.
reviews.text: Nice shady campground, mix of small and larger sites. Clean bathrooms and very handy water bottle filler.

reviews.author: KEN T.
reviews.text: Ranger recommended Perfect campsite (R19) with fairy bridge. Spent a week in great weather for climbing and hiking. Only disappointed was ban on campfires….maybe next time.

reviews.author: Jim B.
reviews.text: nice campground.   NPS employees are fantastic!!

reviews.author: Marty W.
reviews.text: Rangers very helpful great campsite

reviews.author: Donna B.
reviews.text:
We had a nice, spacious site in Loop D. Restrooms were clean. 
In Loop D, which is designated reservation only, all sites had a red “reserved “ sign on the site post, but at least half of them were never occupied. The sign at the campground entrance always said “full”, and we couldn’t help but wonder what kind of a system is in place that allows this. 
No campfires allowed all summer, and I find this to be misguided given this is a maintained, front country campground. While I understand and appreciate the need to lessen the possibility of wildfires, not being able to have a campfire in such campgrounds really takes away from the camping experience. I would be curious to know statistics about the percentage of wildfires originating from such campgrounds???
Not once during our stay of three nights did we ever see a park service employee go through the campground. Sadly, perhaps that was one of the negative impacts of the cuts to the park service.
Quite interestingly however, we were shocked to see a STREET SWEEPER go through the campground multiple times! That was a first, and we were puzzled about that.

reviews.author: Amber C.
reviews.text: Fairly spacious site with the tent pad down a bit lower than the picnic area.  A short walk to the bathrooms and trash is across the way.  There’s a short trail from the campground that will take you to an (easy) trail to Longmire.  A great route to get a nice hike in with a pit stop for coffee or a meal at Longmire.

reviews.author: Amber C.
reviews.text: This site has a tent pad a few stone steps down into a small ditch-like area.  It was great because you don’t get a lot of the light pollution from the bathrooms or headlights.   Note: no soap in the bathrooms, and if the bathroom door is kept open overnight, the sinks are CRAWLING with bugs in the morning.  Overall, good experience with well-spaced sites.

reviews.author: Amber C.
reviews.text: I liked the campground and this campsite.  Sites are well spaced so it doesn’t feel crowded.  This site is across from the bathroom, but not too close.  The bathroom lights did stay on all night, so if you’re sensitive to light when sleeping, this may not be the spot for you.  If the bathroom door is left open overnight, the sinks will be CRAWLING with bugs in the AM.  Note: no soap in the bathrooms.

reviews.author: magen l.
reviews.text: Great campground! Quick drive or pleasant 1.5mi hike down to Longmire. Sites are nice and well kept. Bathrooms and garbage bin area were super clean. Some of the sites are a little small and packed in close to one another while others are large and more secluded.

reviews.author: Jong H.
reviews.text: convenient location to all attractions.

reviews.author: Matthew G.
reviews.text: Stayed at Cougar Rock campground for 2 nights. Camp site and bathrooms were clean and the reservation set up went smoothly. Only complaint I have is our car battery would not start the last morning when we were set to leave. It was a rental so we did not have a jump box or jumper cables. You also have zero cell service inside of and for a few miles outside of the campsite so we could not call anyone for assistance. We asked the ranger for help and he said he could help with making a phone call but I was very surprised that they did not have a jump box inside of the ranger station. It was a fairly large building with electric service. I’m sure it is a fairly common issue with campers and I think it would be a great thing to have with the staff for anyone who has issues, especially since it is so remote. Hopefully the NPS adds it to their on-site equipment in the near future.

reviews.author: Maria S.
reviews.text: The campsites are spacious with trees and shrubbery between them. The parking spots and tent spots were level. The campsite was clean.

reviews.author: Gordon B.
reviews.text: Quiet and nice campground. No frills, easy to find and while most spots were occupied didn’t feel as though people were on top of you.

reviews.author: Bryan T.
reviews.text: Campsite was so small. Not big enough for a tent. No one at office to ask about changing.

reviews.author: Deborah W.
reviews.text: If you have the time, it is worth it to walk over to the Nisqually River. You can experience crossing the river on a log bridge and there is a nice view of Mount Rainier. Another short hike you can access from the campground is the Wonderland trail next to the Nisqually River, which can get you to Longmire (1.7 miles one-way) where there is a store with souvenirs, snacks, and some basic essentials.

reviews.author: Julia  M.
reviews.text: Very good campgrounde, beautyful sites

reviews.author: charles m.
reviews.text: The place was quite, easy access and the staffs were so helpful.  Will be back again

reviews.author: CHIHI C.
reviews.text: Well maintained

reviews.author: Charles B.
reviews.text: Wasn’t sure how I was supposed to get my 8’ teardrop and small suv into my assigned site, but after numerous attempts to get them in, my superior intellect and patience prevailed.  I now appreciate National Park humor.  The view was worth it.

reviews.author: Andrea S.
reviews.text: E3 is a nice site, but not as big or sunny as E1. Unlike E1 though, there is a pull through driveway so you could potentially fit 2 cars at E3.

reviews.author: Andrea S.
reviews.text:
Nice quiet section of the campground. E1 has enough room for 2 tents, but only room for 1 car. Sunny tent pad, not far from the bathroom but not too close. There is a tree next to the site that looks like it may be about to fall so I'd recommend checking that out if its still there when you reserve - I reported it to the campground so they will hopefully inspect it to see if its a hazard.

This campground has flush toilets (no soap in bathrooms though), drinking water, and food storage bins that are bear-proof.

reviews.author: Andrea S.
reviews.text: Right next to the bathroom - i would pick a different site if you have options. There's no blow dryer to create noise but there is an automatic light that turns on and the sound of doors closing.

reviews.author: Wes C.
reviews.text: Was camped at B016. Absolutely beautiful site. It says the pad can only accommodate a 8x10 tent but we easily fit a 14x9. Plenty of room for parking. Not too far from the restrooms either which are kept pretty clean. Would highly recommend to anyone wanting to camp here

reviews.author: Leslie I.
reviews.text: Parking pad was not very level. Site was small and quite far from the bathroom, plus not very private. No place to hang a hammock, but the location of the campground is convenient to Paradise and Longmire areas.

reviews.author: Amanda V.
reviews.text: The campsite was good. It was pretty but it was right next to the bathrooms which meant a lot of ppl going through campsite to get to bathrooms. Great campsite for getting to hikes through out the paradise side of the park. No phone service, fyi

reviews.author: Linnaea  S.
reviews.text: It would be helpful to have Starlink satellite if you plan to make any other internet reservations like purchasing tickets for entry into other areas of the park. The nearest satellite service we could obtain was in the town of Ashford. Areas like Paradise are crowded. Parking is limited. Plan to get up early or visit later in the day after 5pm.

reviews.author: Kegan W.
reviews.text: Best place to camp near Paradise. Nights get loud and bright since the plots are close together, children screaming until 1am and half the block was lit up by many crazy bright flood lights from other campers' vehicles and such. No night patrol means you can't do much to stop it and they didn't care to listen to reason. Black out your tent and bring earplugs and you'll be comfortable.

reviews.author: Aimee L.
reviews.text: Love this campground!!! Clean bathrooms and drinking water available... Also the location is the best!!

reviews.author: James and Lee O.
reviews.text: We really enjoyed our stay at Cougar. Nice variety of sites with good space. We went mid week so it wasn’t really busy or noisy. Great views.

reviews.author: Toru Y.
reviews.text: Parking space was next to each other and not flat. Otherwise very good. Easy access to Paradise in early morning to avoid crowds.

reviews.author: Brendan T.
reviews.text: My campsites were available early. My family and I had a great weekend of camping fun!

reviews.author: Rajoshi B.
reviews.text:
Love the campground, right inside the national park.  It was a reasonably shaded spot. We'll be back here. The restrooms were spotless! Toilet paper was provided. But don't forget to bring your own hand soap. There's a communal food storage, but no individual food storage is available. I asked around and people recommended to simply store things in the car, which seemed a little iffy...
Some campgrounds are smaller than others. The restrooms were a bit of a walk, but didn't bother me much. However, carrying the washing items to and from the washroom/washing station can be a hassle. 
The Wonderland Trail was very close, and we could see Mount Rainier from the campground (just outside the camping spot). It helped us time our skyline trail.
Tip: Restrooms are closer when walking toward the exit.
Con: No campfires allowed.

reviews.author: Andrei C.
reviews.text: This was a nice camp with a great view of the mountains. The only thing I didn’t like was the loud music coming from a group of teenage boys that didn’t even bother to clean up their site before dusk, beer cans all over their site.

reviews.author: Robert S.
reviews.text: Nice campground with good location within the park. Bathrooms were good but could use some hangers for towels and toiletries while using the restrooms.

reviews.author: Christine J.
reviews.text: Lovely campsites. Clean restrooms. Appreciate the E Loop - no generators! Thank you!

reviews.author: Autumn W.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, well maintained facilities with flush toilets and a water bottle filling station next to the restrooms.

reviews.author: Suman P.
reviews.text: Great Campsite!! I have camped in all 3 national park campsites in Rainier and its difficult to pick which one I love the most. We were a group of three and we found a walk-in campsite on Thursday morning.

reviews.author: Rebecca  V.
reviews.text:
Clean. The Rangers were super helpful and friendly.
We used a first come first serve site, and while the entrances posted a sign saying the campgrounds were full as did the sign outside the campground, there were still a handful of sites left for us to choose from. The signs were a bit misleading. Regardless, we enjoyed our stay.

reviews.author: Emily B.
reviews.text: Great views of the mountain and close to many popular hikes

reviews.author: Kim P.
reviews.text: Nice quiet campground

reviews.author: Cindy M.
reviews.text: Cougar Rock was a great home base as we explored Mount Rainier National Park.  I would return there if I was interested in that part of the park.  The park is so huge that I would probably try a different campground just to explore a different area.  But Cougar Rock was close enough for us to hike at Paradise Inn and Longmire Museum areas.  Beautiful waterfalls everywhere along the wonderland trail.

reviews.author: Mark M.
reviews.text: Great campground! Enough room for one standard 4-person tent but not much else.

reviews.author: Corey F.
reviews.text: Site was very spacious! Restrooms were good and really had no issues!

reviews.author: Christina C.
reviews.text: Wonderful space! Bummed that there was a fire ban, but made it work. Lots of space. Not as much privacy, but would rather be here than at a hotel. Close to some of the trails, which was great!

reviews.author: Charles W.
reviews.text: Great location, clean bathrooms and an awesome experience

reviews.author: Navkiran  K.
reviews.text: Very good campsite, we enjoyed a lot …

reviews.author: Amanda G.
reviews.text: Campsites are small. Can’t beat the location!

reviews.author: Robert B.
reviews.text: Not a good campground, and not a good site.  Down in a whole, Up against other sites.   Overall the campground needs a lot of work.  Dump station is not working, no water for filling tanks.  Dumpster enclosures falling down.   sad

reviews.author: Carrie K.
reviews.text:
This campground has the best location to the main area of Paradise which was the most important quality for us!  There were a lot of downed trees and debris on sites. I’m not sure if this was from a more recent storm or if it’s always like that, but it made the sites feel very small and cramped. The facilities were as expected and I very much appreciated the water bottle filler station. The RV dump station was not in service which was disappointing, but I’m sure the issue will be resolved. If you are camping in an RV, the spaces are tight, so make sure you carefully read the description of the site you choose to ensure your equipment fits. 

Overall this campground met our needs and we would come back again!

reviews.author: Alicia K.
reviews.text: Great place to camp with a nice hike across the road, wonderland trailhead.

reviews.author: Hannah M.
reviews.text: Cougar rock is a gorgeous campsite that features everything you could ask for aside from a shower. You can’t go wrong with a single one of the spots and the view is gorgeous, even more gorgeous if you choose to do any of the hikes in the area! I love MT raineer and this campground definitely does it justice.

reviews.author: Quinn C.
reviews.text: We had a great time here! We were able to select our own site and then go to the ranger to pay. We had very friendly campers nearby and the bathrooms were very clean.

reviews.author: Juno V.
reviews.text: Excellent campground! There was a large group of kids with some teen or young adult chaperones taking up a lot of the common space including the street. Aside from that, the campground was perfect. The sites are spacious and everything was clean and well-maintained. Will return!

reviews.author: Kathryn G.
reviews.text: Cougar Rock is always a great place to stay when we go to Mt. Rainier. It is centrally located between Paradise and Longmire so it is very convenient. Don't miss the trail from Cougar Rock down to Longmire and back up - it is a great way to end the day.

reviews.author: Jessica M.
reviews.text: Lovely campsite and easy to access from the park entrance. Bathroom facilities were well maintained and it was a perfect place to stop for an overnight to spend some time at Rainier!

reviews.author: Pierre S.
reviews.text: Enjoyed our stay here and really appreciate this generator free loop. Loved the ranger talk on glaciers.

reviews.author: Aleksandra  F.
reviews.text: It was nice and clean

reviews.author: Janet W.
reviews.text: the site was small, but adequate.

reviews.author: Tabitha S.
reviews.text: Clean sites, kind rangers and staff. Lovely scenery! Sites are close together so prepare to kindly coexist.

reviews.author: Nicole C.
reviews.text: Really loved this campground. Beautiful in all the trees. Sites are pretty close to one another but not too close, and there are so many trees the views to other sites were obstructed so it didn’t feel exposed. Tons of shade. Plenty of room for tents at our site D32. The main tent spot was a bit downhill so in heavy rain we would have set up the tent closer to the picnic table and car, on higher ground. Bathrooms not too far, no soap. Fire ban when we were there in July. 20min to Paradise Visitors Center and the many hikes in that area (unless there are construction delays). No bear locker at any specific sites from what I could tell, the signs say to just leave food locked in the car. We did that with no issues, but there did seem to be maybe one big bear locker in each loop as an alternative.

reviews.author: Donna McBain E.
reviews.text: Liked having the rangers at the entry.  Night time talk on mosses and lichen was fun.

reviews.author: Su C.
reviews.text: Kimberly at the Ranger station was very accommodating in getting us a FF site that was lovely and perfect for our 21’ trailer.  Several hikes right out of the campground. Bathrooms and garbage bins close by and the sites were far enough apart to not be able to hear your neighbor’s conversations.  Our site had both sun and shade and was very level.

reviews.author: Roland C.
reviews.text: Excellent rangers and clean bathrooms at a quiet and beautiful corner of the world!

reviews.author: Caitlin C.
reviews.text: Perfect campground with beautiful views. It was great being so close to the Paradise area. Very close to the Longmire area as well with a gift shop and restaurant.

reviews.author: Tim E.
reviews.text: A loop is all first come first serve so there is nearly always availability, river access is across the street

reviews.author: Jennifer  B.
reviews.text: Very large campground but sites were big so you felt like you had room. Great FF and they start selling them early. Get to where your going on the mountain early to get parking and beat the crowds.

reviews.author: Lynn G.
reviews.text: Well maintained. Decent privacy between sites. Close to activities.

reviews.author: Marcia B.
reviews.text: Very large campground.  Site C23 was private, very large, and across from the restroom.  I would book this site again.  Also, two good trees for my hammock.

reviews.author: Andrew K.
reviews.text: NPS needs to get into that campground and pull some of those downed trees out, seems like a tinderbox, especially with irresponsible campers and their campfires.

reviews.author: Page M.
reviews.text: All the park staff were great.

reviews.author: Brodie L.
reviews.text: Make sure to know when campsite releases are and have fun at this treasure of a park I had an incredible experience here!

reviews.author: YIQING Z.
reviews.text: This is the cleanest washroom I’ve ever seen!

reviews.author: Laura L.
reviews.text: Nice campsite! Great proximity to Paradise and trails in the park.

reviews.author: Akshay R.
reviews.text: Really enjoyed the camp ground. Facilities were great.

reviews.author: Douglas C.
reviews.text: Nice

reviews.author: Alejandro G.
reviews.text: We were able to get a spot two days in advance. Nice spots, clean bathrooms!

reviews.author: Kristen M.
reviews.text: Great spot with a view of the mountain. Convenient location, spacious campsites.

reviews.author: Ean M.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground in very natural woods. Located near most interesting sites like Longmont, Paradise, and Stevens Canyon. Pull through was not level.

reviews.author: Andrea S.
reviews.text: Great sites

reviews.author: Jugjit J.
reviews.text: The Campground is very clean, The Park Rangers that I have met when entering the Park are always very nice and professional and always give me helpful information.

reviews.author: Hazel Mae L.
reviews.text: Great campground!

reviews.author: Jill S.
reviews.text: Site E14 was one of the best in the E loop! It is tucked away on its own, away from adjacent sites, and has a 2-tiered set-up. Super nice! (The tent pad is on the smaller side, so just double check if you happen to have a big tent.) I would also strongly recommend E6 and E8, both of which descend via steps to a very private spot in the "valley" within the loop. If you don't want to be close to neighbors, avoid 16, 17, 18, and 19. The whole loop is generator-free, though, which is awesome!

reviews.author: Yuyang Z.
reviews.text: Stayed at the camp site during first-come first-serve season and there are plently of empty site everyday. The check in is very easy as long as you arrive early in the morning to pay and select the site in their office. I wish they would update the fire ban on their official site as we end up staying wet with no campfires.

reviews.author: Otavio P.
reviews.text: Welcoming staff and place was perfect for a pop up tent in a Jeep!

reviews.author: Lukas E.
reviews.text: Rangers - Josh and Reece - were super friendly and filled with great advice! Campsite clean, quiet, bathroom was fine. Stayed three nights here!

reviews.author: Drew K.
reviews.text: Nice bathroom, coinvent location, unfortunately about 10 years ago there was a wild fire which seems to have cleared out a lot of the small trees and vegetation.  This leaves the sites a bit open/exposed, hopefully it fills in a bit in the next few years.

reviews.author: Jennifer B.
reviews.text: This was a nice spot. Good flat ground for car camping. Bathrooms were pretty clean. Saw lots of wild life

reviews.author: Janine V.
reviews.text:
A very lovely place to be. We had a stay at the end of the season. We had a pull through campside with a 30 feet RV. It is better if you get help by a passender by entering or leaving the site. We enjoyed the silence an pure nature. A good stay if you visit the NP. Reservation ist necessary. 
The only negative: No mobile network and no wifi
The Ranger at the reception was very friendly an helpful.

reviews.author: Kaylea C.
reviews.text: Great spot, close to a bunch of good hikes and clean bathrooms.

reviews.author: Thomas G.
reviews.text:
it was late in the season, mid week and First Come First served but very few people so our experience might not be typical of most6 campers.  

The rangers were helpful, the campsite was quiet. It would be nice if there was a dump station and water fill at the campground though.

reviews.author: Cassie S.
reviews.text: Campground was very clean, including the bathrooms, and peaceful.  I didn't know if I should expect showers but there were not-- I might have just not looked adequately when selecting this campground though. No complaints. Very happy to stay here and be able to start my hike first thing in the morning already in the park avoiding all the traffic. 10/10.

reviews.author: Mark W.
reviews.text: Conveniently located next to some fun filler hiking trails as well as one of the lodges.  Facilities were fine and first come first serve was really appreciated.

reviews.author: Richard T.
reviews.text: Restrooms not clean

reviews.author: Carl O.
reviews.text: Host was very helpful. Campsites were clean and spacious. Bathroom was typical, a bit worn and dated but otherwise clean. Very convenient location to see Mt Rainier.

reviews.author: Brooke P.
reviews.text: Great campground. Walking distance to some hikes.

reviews.author: Sandra N.
reviews.text: Great campground. Clean, spaced out well, flushable toilets and convenient access to everything Paradise has to offer. I would definitely camp here again.

reviews.author: Sunil S.
reviews.text: Great place for camping and visiting National Park. Tap water was fresh and good to drink. And it is inside National Park.

reviews.author: Tamy L.
reviews.text: Stayed there on a weekday after Labor Day weekend.  Able to obtain a campsite right away.  Quiet throughout the night.  Has bear box, grille (this was restricted due to fire risk), picnic table.  Bathroom has mirrors, paper towels, flush toilets. Easy access to trail heads in the Longmire area.

reviews.author: Brian S.
reviews.text:
Camping Facilities were clean.  We chose campsite A-10.  Fairly level and easily held our 8ftx9ft tent.
Park Rangers were awesome!  Very helpful and informative!
Very close drive to Paradise Visitors Center (20 minutes)
Just across the road from Cougar Rock Campground is the Wonderland Trail.  Incredible mountain view and walk along the Nisqually and Paradise Rivers on the easy to moderate hike. You can hike up 1.1 miles to the Carter and Madcap Falls. Hike an additional 1.5 miles past Carter Falls to see Narada Falls.  (or you can access trailheads via your vehicle on drive to Paradise Visitors Center, but the trailhead parking areas can be crowded in the afternoons)   Recommend doing Reflection Lake early morning as the Sun is behind you and the wind is usually calm that time of day for best pictures.  Tons of hikes originate from Paradise Visitors Center.

reviews.author: Kirk R.
reviews.text: Nice clean, quiet, beautiful campsite. The check-in ranger was very friendly and helpful. We really enjoyed our stay.

reviews.author: G M.
reviews.text: The campsite was small, and close to other sites around it leaving little space for privacy. But the site and campground was clean and well maintained. Restrooms were also clean and well maintained. Trails nearby were excellent.

reviews.author: Matthew B.
reviews.text: The campground was very clean, and quiet at night, no biting insects to be seen. I appreciate that even though the campground was quite full, I didn't have to hear any generators or music. It seems like every site around me had a bear box, which was very convenient. It was plenty of space to store my food box, water, and cooler. My tent pad was clean and level, very easy and comfortable. The bathrooms are in good condition. Easy access to walking trails.

reviews.author: Naomi O.
reviews.text: We arrived Saturday morning at 9am (9am timed entry) on Labor Day Weekend with little hope that there would be a first-come spot available. We went right to the campground and got the second to last spot available! So lucky! They took credit card payment - $20. Just a heads up - spot A26 is lovely but the light from the bathroom across from it was glaring into our campsite all night (doesn't go off). We parked a car sideways in our site to block out most of the light, but it wasn't ideal. Still, the stars were INCREDIBLE. I can't wait to go back next year - will be trying to reserve ahead this time.

reviews.author: Taylor J.
reviews.text: Very clean and peaceful!

reviews.author: Roberta T.
reviews.text: The campground is very conveniently located to access trails and Paradise. Excellent education talks are organized by rangers during weekends. The staff is accommodating and nice. The toilets could be cleaner, but we love coming to this campground and have been doing this for the last three years.

reviews.author: Robert Y.
reviews.text: Very accessible to many pats of the National Park; very large parking area for 2 vehicles; very friendly staff.

reviews.author: Romeo D.
reviews.text: Great camping site. My kids enjoy our stay. Neighborhood site is respectful and quite feels like we owned the whole national park. Kudos!

reviews.author: Kaylee B.
reviews.text: It was an amazing campground ♥️

reviews.author: Corrinne H.
reviews.text: Great campground! We had plenty of trees around our site and it was quiet at night. We hiked to Carter and Madcap Falls from the campground too, and really appreciated the close access to the trailhead just across the street. The ranger talk in the evening was also great. Would stay again! Loved the proximity to Paradise for hiking, too.

reviews.author: Natalie  B.
reviews.text: Really nice, big camp ground. Toilets were very clean. Great location.

reviews.author: Hung P.
reviews.text: Big spot, short walk to bathroom which were clean, campsite was nice and quiet in the evening. Close to Carter's Falls trail which was nice.

reviews.author: Hung P.
reviews.text: Bathrooms were clean and near the campsite. Site was permitted for 15ft rig but we had a 19ft rig that fit just right. Close to the next campsite but not overbearing. Quiet a night. Not much more you can ask for.

reviews.author: Lyle B.
reviews.text: Great location, restrooms were clean. We were close to the restrooms so lots of people kept walking through out campsite to get to the restrooms. Trash bins were convenient. Good hiking close by.

reviews.author: Karli F.
reviews.text: wonderful camp site

reviews.author: Lyle R.
reviews.text: Lovely campground which has been ignored. A crew needs to come in and clean out all the downed tree debris. Something also needs to change with regards to cancellations, so many unused campsites, so sad for those who are unable to procure a site.

reviews.author: David P.
reviews.text: This is a great campground with an excellent support staff.  Considering how heavily it is used, it is amazing that they are able to keep it so clean and the sites so well maintained.  Loved our stay.

reviews.author: Jeanyves P.
reviews.text: Great camp host. Beautiful campground and clean restrooms.

reviews.author: Andrea  B.
reviews.text: Clean bathrooms, good views of Rainier, star gazing. Dishwashing sinks are super helpful. No cell reception. Tent sites are often tiny tiny.

reviews.author: Gregory G.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our stay in loop d. The facilities were clean and the campground was quiet. The evening ranger talk was interesting and well planned.

reviews.author: Eli C.
reviews.text: Very quiet and wonderful pines.  Good hiking nearby.

reviews.author: Jan M.
reviews.text: no views of the mountain from campground, but super short drive to views/Paradise/hiking

reviews.author: Paul H.
reviews.text: Clean, quiet campground. Sites are nicely separated. Enjoyed my stay!

reviews.author: Victoria J.
reviews.text: Great campsite and great location. Particularly appreciated the flush toilets and clean rest rooms

reviews.author: John  L.
reviews.text: excellent staff encounter and campground no issues

reviews.author: Bruce C.
reviews.text: Great location for south west portion of the park.  Very heavily wooded

reviews.author: Steve R.
reviews.text: We enjoyed camping here very much. Beautiful location and convenient to hiking in the park. The road noise was not very noticiable during the day and quieted down completely after dark. Facilities were clean and the rangers were very helpful.

reviews.author: Spencer N.
reviews.text: Only bad mark was that it wasn't super clear what to do for folks who get there late at night. Besides that, the campground is beautiful and we loved the all day access to the park the morning after our check-in date.

reviews.author: Ash L.
reviews.text: Nice flat campsite, fire pit (burn ban was in effect though), and bear box. Fit our 4 person tent (7x9) in the elevated area, could probably fit a slightly bigger tent too. Had to walk through another (vacant) campsite to get to the C loop bathrooms. Bathrooms were good enough, and there were water fountains outside. There are some bugs so bring bug spray. Nice drive up to Paradise and Reflection Lake for stargazing.

reviews.author: jennielyn o.
reviews.text: Very accessible

reviews.author: Yakelin  B.
reviews.text: Nice and clean restrooms. Lots of available restrooms and garbage cans. Some sites are too close together but many offer some distance. We want wait to go back!

reviews.author: Katrina R.
reviews.text: Our campsite was great until it started to rain - all the water pooled under our tent and all around the site so there was nowhere else to move our tent. There wasn’t any way to drain the water off, and it was several inches deep by the time we packed up and left. E026 would be great for any trip that doesn’t have a forecast for rain.

reviews.author: Mouni N.
reviews.text: Such a great campsite. We had D loop 9 and 10. A good combo for two families would be D10 and D34. Then you could pass through for bathroom access.

reviews.author: Richard G.
reviews.text:
Only difficulty was when we tried to go up to  Summerland from Cougar rock. As they are in different quadrants of the park a 'timed entry' permit was needed. Unfortunately there is no internet provider in the park, therefore no way to apply for a permit. Only way we could transit to the summerland quadrant was to rise before 4:30 AM and arrive before 7:00 AM at the summerland entrance. 

Surely the park can do better for people who are already camping within Mt Rainier Park!!

reviews.author: Kevin W.
reviews.text: Always a great stay in Cougar Rock campground. Beautiful area and lot's to see and do

reviews.author: Addie  L.
reviews.text: Tiny little campsite (big enough for my 1-man tent) next to trash bins on one side and downhill from the bathrooms on the other; there was pretty constant movement and a lot more light in my tent than usual. Otherwise, nice campground! BUT--if there's no fire warning, be aware that they will cheat the PANTS off of you on wood prices: $15 for a tiny bundle (I saw $8 at White River Campground a couple days later). The attendant literally said to me, "It's cheaper outside the park, but most people don't wanna drive out and wait in line to enter again." Nice of him to explain price-gouging to me. It seems incredibly shortsighted of the campground/park not to offer fair prices if they don't want people to bring in their own wood from more than 50 miles away.

reviews.author: Tianyi X.
reviews.text: Very nice. Clean and dry. Restroom nearby.

reviews.author: Greg B.
reviews.text: Leveling our 19-foot travel trailer on site D35 was a bit challenging.  However, we were able to find a location that worked.

reviews.author: FNU S.
reviews.text: Really good camping experience at the campground. Nice campsite, good ranger programs and the national park is obviously beautiful. If there were 1-2 more washrooms, that would be great.

reviews.author: Amy V.
reviews.text: Overall Campground was good, quiet. Our tent site B24 was a little small and not much space. We had two very small tents and felt like we were right up against the fire pit and very close to the narrow road way. Our site was suppose to be good for 6 ppl but it’s more comfortable for 2-3 ppl max

reviews.author: MARISA V.
reviews.text: lots of trees and most campsites have share, clean bathrooms, no showers, not far from Paradise are where they have breakfast and lunch there, also not far from Longmire, with restaurant at the INN, you can get Ice there.

reviews.author: Mickey H.
reviews.text: Really enjoyed the ranger program, the kindness of the lady helping us with the reservations, our shady spot, and the clean bathrooms. Thank you!

reviews.author: Caroline H.
reviews.text: Great experience in camping at a first come spot on loop A.  The park ranger was friendly. The campground was busy yet quiet.  Overall, great experience!

reviews.author: Cassandra S.
reviews.text: Very nice campground

reviews.author: Angel S.
reviews.text: Excellent place to camp

reviews.author: Ruth Ann D.
reviews.text: Such a great stay! Short walk to some beautiful spots. Bathrooms were well maintained.

reviews.author: Khursheed K.
reviews.text: Fantastic experience with the staff at entry and at the campground. Pauline was fabulous!

reviews.author: Leah C.
reviews.text: Great campground close to Paradise. Clean restrooms. No cell service.

reviews.author: Clairie M.
reviews.text:
Excellent campsite. We had a great time there. The only downside I need to say - and please consider it - was the toilet situation! That was horrible.
No toilet paper. Only two sinks and one of them was not working at all and they were very dirty. Please, do something about it.

reviews.author: Kurtis A.
reviews.text: Cougar Rock campground was a great place to stay on our trip to Mount Rainer. The drive to the campground is spectacular. The restrooms were relatively clean, but you could tell their age. The sites are pretty close to each other. I would recommend ear plugs if you are a light sleeper; young kids with us up early in the morning. The proximity of this campground to popular hikes makes choosing this site a no brainer. Overall, this is a great campground and I would recommend it.

reviews.author: Richard S.
reviews.text: Nice site, clean restrooms, dish washing station and wonderful checkin ranger.

reviews.author: Daniel C.
reviews.text:
Staff at check in were very friendly and polite. Also helpful in directing us to a near by trail head . 
The bathroom is very old and not ADA compliant. The toilet stalls are not big enough for someone to access in a wheelchair!!

reviews.author: Darcy F.
reviews.text:
Cougar Rock campground was a pleasant little surprise! We loved the trees and our spot was absolutely perfect. It had a lot of room and was A pull through site. A short walk to the bathrooms.
My kids and I woke up early one morning and made the short drive to Paradise to hike the skyline trail at sunrise. This was one of the highlights of our whole trip!

reviews.author: Benny  Q.
reviews.text: The staff were very friendly, especially my young man with the last name Hahn.  We came in on first come first serve and got a good spot.  There were a variety of campers and trailer sizes all around us. Relatively clean bathroom. The dish room was super handy. The water pump was great.

reviews.author: Jennifer J.
reviews.text: We loved the whole experience! We hiked up at Paradise for several days in early July. I'd probably recommend coming a bit later in July/August because the wildflowers would be amazing then!  Be sure to get up early to get a parking spot at Paradise!

reviews.author: Melanie G.
reviews.text: We fit with our 25’ travel trailer. It was a little unlevel but nothing crazy. One tight turn in the loop but it was alright. Amazing campground- very close to overlooks and Paradise, huckleberries in the campground and a fun ranger program one night. We will be back

reviews.author: Sarah L.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Well maintained, quiet, and felt very safe. No cell service for TMobile. The rangers were friendly and we will come back again!

reviews.author: Dana Y.
reviews.text: Very nice sites with green belt separating sites. overall pleasant experience.

reviews.author: Audrey E.
reviews.text: X

reviews.author: Bruce T.
reviews.text: Nice campground.  We were in a spacious quiet site at the end of Loop C.

reviews.author: Lenka S.
reviews.text: The campground wasn’t as beautiful as other campgrounds we visited this year. The campsites were very close to each other and some people were making noise. But the restrooms weren’t far away and were clean.

reviews.author: John S.
reviews.text: I felt very fortunate to get a campsite, especially because I had to wait until after 3 pm to get into the park because my timed entry was for the wrong corridor.  The campground was quiet and I could ride my bike up to the Paradise visitors center from my site.

reviews.author: Xu G.
reviews.text: Great campground in a very decent National Park, Clean washrooms, drinkable water provided.

reviews.author: katherine w.
reviews.text:
This is a beautiful campground!! Very quiet a d peaceful. . Great rangers. Fun informative ranger programs. 
Clean restrooms! I hope to return next year. Thank you!

reviews.author: Laima V.
reviews.text: We spent only a couple of nights, but really enjoyed our stay. It had everything we needed - flat spot for the tent, bbq racks, table and benches, bathroom. Campsite nestled between trees, temperature felt a little higher over the night than the rest of the park.

reviews.author: Kerry O.
reviews.text: Great campground…clean bathrooms, really enjoyed my time there

reviews.author: Olaf S.
reviews.text: It was very quiet with only a little campfire smoke.  (Smoke is irritating, so less of it is better.)  It was easy to get there, even though we had to enter the Paradise corridor.

reviews.author: Anna T.
reviews.text: The amazing location 20 mins from Paradise is the main reason to go here. Sadly, the forest seemed rather unhealthy with a lot of dead trees around the campsites. There's also no individual bear boxes. Bathrooms were fairly clean though.

reviews.author: Lisa H.
reviews.text: Nice campground

reviews.author: David G.
reviews.text: toilets in excellent shape , campsite clean and as expected. would recommend as a good national park campground

reviews.author: Bret K.
reviews.text: When we visited Cougar Rock the dump station was closed and has been for while and there was no fresh water to fill our water tanks.  Spots are ok for Vans and smaller units. Big Units have little to no chance of fitting in most of the spaces.

reviews.author: Man N.
reviews.text: Pull through site but wasn't level.  Still usable for a campervan.  Site itself was good and clean.  No reception for T-Mobile or Verizon.

reviews.author: Terry  M.
reviews.text: Great Campground easy to access near everything you want to see at Mount Rainier

reviews.author: Catherine A.
reviews.text: Views of Mt Rainier from the campground, not super flat but pretty, some shade.

reviews.author: Cynthia K.
reviews.text: Many pull through sites that were moderately level. Access to several trails was available from the campground.

reviews.author: Eda A.
reviews.text: Great experience!

reviews.author: Nikolas J.
reviews.text: Fantastic campground, quiet and friendly. Would absolutely recommended if you are staying in the park. A quick drive to Paradise, obviously further to the Sunset side of things but an amazing drive down that direction across the park. Awesome hikes very easily accessible from the campground.

reviews.author: Sydney P.
reviews.text: Great location, clean, quiet, has plenty of water/bathrooms. Sites are tight but I appreciate how efficient they are with so many people visiting the park. A and R loops are the only first come first serve areas so glance at a map before you arrive (especially if arriving in the dark). No cell service until Paradise but 5G once there.

reviews.author: Mason L.
reviews.text: Such a lovely, wooded location inside the park. Only a 20 minute drive from paradise!

reviews.author: Sydney M.
reviews.text: The campground host was so kind and helpful. The sites and restrooms are very well kept and the grounds are absolutely beautiful!

reviews.author: Anna L.
reviews.text: It was a great campground with a great location near paradise. Really enjoyed camping next to a volcano and all the amenities that the campground offered. I would defiantly camp here again if I’m ever in the area.

reviews.author: Kris W.
reviews.text: Great proximity to the Wonderland Trail and other trails for all ages and abilities.

reviews.author: Julie D.
reviews.text:
Pros: with reservations you won’t need to pay to get into the park.  It’s in a very good location close to popular trails. The bathrooms are clean. 

Cons: you’ll have a hard time finding a site that can accommodate an 8 person tent. Most are suitable for 2-4 person tents.

reviews.author: Xilin Y.
reviews.text:
The camp gerund is pretty well-maintained with clean flush toilets, potable water fountain, convenient flushable waste disposal sink (for washing dishes). It’s close to paradise and the visitor center and a few nice falls. The only thing is their wood is very expensive at 15 per bundle and cash only after 4pm when the ranger gets offduty. 

The campsite itself is a bit small, so the limitation on tent and car size actually make sense. Pretty nice overall.

reviews.author: Marcus F.
reviews.text: Great site in this loop. Lots of space (we have a 28' MH and a CRV toad) on this pull through. Excellent Starlink. Only complaint is the dump station is out of order and there is nowhere to dump within 30 miles according to the ranger. We strictly rationed the waste water generation and got through 5 days. The bathhouse does have disposal sinks that you can cart a few gallons of gray over to.

reviews.author: Michele A.
reviews.text: Great campground !!

reviews.author: David B.
reviews.text: Very wooded and quiet campground.  Exactly what I wanted.

reviews.author: Nathaniel C.
reviews.text: The campsite itself was not great. Trees were cut down, there was a rotted stump in the middle of the campground and it was a tough place to be when it rained for two days straight.  Other than that, I always enjoy the hard work the workers provide and they are always professional, but this campsite was awful.

reviews.author: Albert S.
reviews.text: Be aware if you use a tent, the tent pad is much too close to the fire pit to build a fire.

reviews.author: Albert S.
reviews.text: Cougar Rock is a wonderful campground with easy access to Paradise Visitor Center. My husband and I have been camping here for over 30 years. In the last several years the campground seems to cater more to RVs rather than those of us that still tent camp. If you tent camp be aware that this site has a large boulder sitting on the left side of the tent pad. We had to set our REI Dome on the boulder and only use the right side of the tent.

reviews.author: Mike S.
reviews.text: Nice campground but it needs some love. Also the campground was understaffed, only one person that was way overworked and he was dealing with way too long of a line of walk up campers trying to check in.

reviews.author: Anjeli D.
reviews.text: Spent the weekend in Mount Rainier National Park in early October & had a great stay at Cougar Rock Campground. We came mid-afternoon on a Friday & a number of camping spots were still open. The campground manager was kind & assigned us a spot near the river after I asked if there was one nearby. The campground was clean & well taken care-of, with full working bathrooms & clean running water. Remember to bring your own firewood, as foraging for wood on wilderness land damages the ecosystem (and isn't allowed). The campground sold firewood bundles, but they close at 5pm so come early if that's something you need. So grateful to have nice facilities to enjoy a beautiful weekend in nature!

reviews.author: Jeff F.
reviews.text:
Cougar Rock campsite A11 (Loop A) isn't an ideal "tent" campsite.  The pad for the tent is only 30-40 yards from the main road leading up to Paradise - lots of traffic.  In addition, the position of the campsite in relationship to the Loop A access road stinks . . .     (It is in the direct line of all on-coming vehicles; and, after dark, I can't tell you how many times I was blinded by some bonehead with his/her/their bright lights on . . . )   My buddy and I scoped out the other loops available in the Cougar Rock Campground and will definitely be choosing Loop B, Loop C or Loop D in the future.

On the other hand, the Rangers on duty around 2:00 p.m., Thursday, October 5 were great . . .

reviews.author: Raegan H.
reviews.text: it was good

reviews.author: Adawna W.
reviews.text: We love Cougar Rock.  We usually camp at the end of the season because it is less crowded.  Staff are helpful and friendly

reviews.author: Caroline W.
reviews.text: great campground; first come first served worked well for me. I was able to accomplish numerous hikes from this location; my favorite was Comet Falls/Van Trump Park. The rangers were exceedingly friendly and well-informed.

reviews.author: Jason L.
reviews.text: Great rangers, great campground

reviews.author: mike m.
reviews.text: Very clean. Very organized. There was a Burn Ban so no campfires.

reviews.author: Jonni  R.
reviews.text: Got there early and had a great spot. Super helpful Ranger!

reviews.author: Hunter B.
reviews.text: Great camp grounds! The sites and facilities were clean and well kept. The sites weren’t too close to each other.

reviews.author: Sophie T.
reviews.text: Lovely campground with good-sized campsites (parking space is limited). Clean bathrooms. Conveniently-placed water sources. The park rangers who checked me in were friendly and helpful. I even got free firewood! This is a great placed campground for exploring the Paradise Area of the park.

reviews.author: Mark W.
reviews.text: Good camp site, no complaints. Staff was very nice and helpful

reviews.author: Stephanie K.
reviews.text: Site E2 was overall a great site. Had privacy from other sites, was flat, and had adequate space for our tents and hammock. Close enough to a bathroom, but not too close. It is a corner site, so it is along the campground road, but this was not an issue. My only complaint is I wish the site had an individual bear box, but there was one available in front of the bathroom.

reviews.author: Sofie A.
reviews.text: Beautiful, clean, and quiet campground right nearby many trails and around a 20 minute drive from Paradise viewpoint. We did the Skyline Loop Trail which had amazing and clear views that day! Fall in Rainier is gorgeous

reviews.author: Jay L.
reviews.text: Cougar Rock Campground was amazing! I was especially impressed with the dishwashing station that was available for use at the restroom. Definitely head up to Paradise and hike some of the trails that are up there, including the Dead Horse Trail. The waterfalls are also beautiful in the area so check those out too!

reviews.author: Chris R.
reviews.text: Good personnel, lots of nice clean campsites.

reviews.author: Mary H.
reviews.text: Great place

reviews.author: Dominique P.
reviews.text: Very satisfied with Cougar Rock Campground.

reviews.author: Madison J.
reviews.text: This camp ground was very close to Paradise at Mount Rainier. The camp spot was very open and you could see so many stars at night. They have a bathroom and dump station in each loop. The spaces weren't too close to one another and the rangers on site were very nice.

reviews.author: Henry S.
