reviews.text: Stayed two nights (on separate loops as we stayed an extra night ) and both plots were level and well sized for our needs. Toilets were clean and tidy. Staff helpful as ever. Good site to go up to Paradise - Mount Rainier and Reflection Lake, both about 15 minutes by vehicle.

reviews.author: Bob T.
reviews.text: ghsfjsfj

reviews.author: Jean K.
reviews.text: Enjoyed camping here.  Definitely not for big rigs.  Ours was 24 ft and was fine. Good base camp for visiting Paradise.  The best alpine hiking that we have experienced. Note to get to the visitor centre in Paradise early to secure a parking spot.

reviews.author: Dennis M.
reviews.text: We really enjoyed the campground and its amenities.  Very convenient to all the sites.

reviews.author: Joanna P.
reviews.text: This campground has some pretty rustic elements. My first site was like a walk-in site, though it wasn't marked as one... the "long driveway" shown on the map was actually a very short driveway then a trail up to the picnic table, which was a bummer as I have some mobility issues. The site was marked as a tent site, but didn't have a level spot for a tent. Overall the campground feels rough and a bit dated, but the bathrooms were at least average cleanliness and I love that they had ranger programs 3 nights a week. I had no cell service on any of the 3 major carriers but there was excellent service if you were willing to drive up to Paradise.

reviews.author: Candice M.
reviews.text: In a decent location in the park. Could have been taken care of a little bit more but manageable.

reviews.author: Misty H.
reviews.text: Campsites are small, but the campground is nice and in a good location.

reviews.author: David L.
reviews.text:
At Cougar Rock:
We were informed we could bring no pets.  Multiple other campsites brought their dogs. 
We were informed we could have no campfires. Multiple other campsites set up campfires. 

Look, I understand there are reasons for no pets and no campfires, but please drive around at 9 pm to enforce these rules if you're going to have them.

reviews.author: Lucky B.
reviews.text: Great campground in the park itself!

reviews.author: Abigail  L.
reviews.text: Check in staff was great. Great location and so quiet after a long day of hiking

reviews.author: Courtney C.
reviews.text: Great spot! Well-kept, good location, good spacing between sites. Bathrooms are clean and there is potable water. A little more concrete than expected where we had to place our tent, so definitely recommend some sleeping pads. The view of the mountain is incredible, too. And there is a cool trail with a river crossing just across the street.

reviews.author: Kurt K.
reviews.text: It is nice to be close to Mt. Rainer for a few days, but after that I would plan on hitting the road. Very busy park with lots of people, so you have to do your homework to escape the crowds.

reviews.author: Colleen F.
reviews.text: The campground and facilities were so clean! We enjoyed having some space between the sites as well. Perfect first camping trip for our son (4 months!).

reviews.author: Qinglin M.
reviews.text: Cougar Rock Campground is very nice. Each site is big and private. They are surrounded by tall trees and tent pad is nicely built. The amphitheater  is beautiful and the ranger program that I attended about the night light and sound was informative and entertaining. The only drawback is that there is no shower facility and the bathroom was too far to walk for some sites including mine.

reviews.author: Christopher R.
reviews.text: Great location to the skyline trail. Cleanish bathroom. Very quiet despite neighboring sites pretty close.

reviews.author: Stephanie H.
reviews.text: This is a lively campground, great sites, quiet and would definitely stay there again.  What was exceptionally nice was the fire ban, a smoke free campground is wonderful for those that don’t enjoy the smoke.

reviews.author: Jenny Rae B.
reviews.text: Perfect spot to camp in the park. Bathrooms and water were easily accessible and campsites were cozy and well maintained.

reviews.author: ROBERT C.
reviews.text: Site A14 had a large flat tent site that took tent stakes well, and a picnic table and bear box both in good repair. Parking area was of appropriate size. Only (very minor) complaint was a pothole on one side of parking area where it adjoined the road, but it was easily avoided. Enjoyed 2 days of hiking through awesome country while there.

reviews.author: DANIEL T.
reviews.text: Awesome

reviews.author: Dorothy R.
reviews.text: Got lucky and got a walk in tent site right away.

reviews.author: John F.
reviews.text: Wonderful campsite close to hiking to nearby waterfall and the river. Unfortunately wildfire smoke obscured some of the views.

reviews.author: Randall A.
reviews.text: Please do not allow campfires!

reviews.author: Caledonia G.
reviews.text: If you are planning to camp at cougar rock on the weekend and are looking for a first come first serve campsite, I recommend getting there by 7 am! The rangers were all super friendly, helpful and kind, and the campsite was only a 15 minute drive to paradise and all the trails that start from the Henry M Jackson Memorial visitor center. I can’t wait to come back.

reviews.author: Valentina w.
reviews.text: Beautiful area but campsites are very close with little foliage to give a sense of privacy

reviews.author: Benjamin L.
reviews.text: Easy breezy

reviews.author: Will D.
reviews.text: Great campground. You'd think with how big it is that you'd be crossing paths with lots of other people, but it felt like we had our own, quiet space despite being close to the campground's road. Good bathrooms, fire pit, picnic tables, and just a beautiful place.

reviews.author: Sharon D.
reviews.text:
The campground was great! The bathrooms were clean with flush toilets, soap, space to put your toiletry bag, and very accessible. with the trail shortcuts around, it was easy to be close to multiple bathrooms. the campsite had sufficient space for our tent and car. the location of the campground is very close to some beautiful lakes that are worth to checkout, specifically during sunset. 

Overall, it is what I expected a clean campground would be like :)

reviews.author: Daniel R.
reviews.text: Very nice campground if you can get a spot!

reviews.author: Justin  D.
reviews.text: We had a great time at Cougar Rock Campground. The sites were sufficiently spaced, the bathrooms were always clean and stocked with toilet paper and paper towels, and the park rangers were friendly. We could see Mt. Rainier from the front of our site (E022) and the stars at night were incredible! We really enjoyed the hike up Narada Falls and Lake Louise was a great spot for swimming. The only complaint I have is about the available firewood. You have to buy it from the gift shop in Longmire and it was $15 for a small bundle. Definitely pick some up in Ashford if you intend to have a campfire.

reviews.author: deirdre s.
reviews.text: Mount rainier national park was wonderful.  Cougar creek was a good campground as a base for great hikes in Paradise area.  Very quiet.  Appreciate bear box.  Dish washing facilities and showers would be much appreciated

reviews.author: Myckaela H.
reviews.text: the location was great, we were able to hit some hikes early in the morning before the crowds came. downside is how close everyone is. we were in site B27. the first night we didn’t sleep because the people right next to us had a dog barking and were talking extremely loud. however, the next night was great as some people left and it was super quiet. it really depends on who you’re by and if the sites around you are occupied. i do not recommended if you prefer private and off grid camping, but if you can overlook that for proximity to the park then it’s a good option. tent dimensions say 5x7 but we easily fit our 7x9 tent. a perk of this specific site is that the trees block the view from the road so it added some privacy.

reviews.author: Daina R.
reviews.text: Nice quiet campground. Bathrooms were clean.

reviews.author: Daniel G.
reviews.text: Wish the cg was closer to paradise

reviews.author: Ehsan H.
reviews.text: Great campground. Very close to paradise

reviews.author: Andrew B.
reviews.text: Campsite was in a nice central spot and was well kept, however there were large log rounds from fell trees everywhere, limiting space. Additionally, this is definitely a 1 tent site, not a 2 as advertised in the site description. 1 4-person tent barely fit into the tent area.

reviews.author: Richard G.
reviews.text: Good overall. Rather a long trip to the washrooms, which were not well cleaned

reviews.author: Emily N.
reviews.text: Nice campground.

reviews.author: Rikako W.
reviews.text: Great, quiet campsite. Not the most secluded, but it gave us a great place to stay. I wish the bathroom was closer than walking for 5 minutes, though.

reviews.author: Maddy P.
reviews.text: Great location!

reviews.author: Delaine J.
reviews.text: great location

reviews.author: Cedric M.
reviews.text: Very friendly hosts, clean facilities, nice clean campsite.

reviews.author: Ethan Y.
reviews.text: Great site with easy access to the Paradise section of the park. Average scenery—nothing out of this world. Bathrooms were a bit older but in good condition.

reviews.author: Erin S.
reviews.text: I had a great experience at Cougar Rock. It's cheap, so don't expect a lot of frills. I managed to get a first-come-first-serve spot two nights in a row mid-week in August. Rangers were extremely kind and helpful. As a solo camper I felt safe and comfortable here.

reviews.author: Kevin  B.
reviews.text: Nice campsite.   Volunteers at the registration booth were very helpful. A+.

reviews.author: Gillian C.
reviews.text: Loop E was quiet which was appreciated.

reviews.author: Justine B.
reviews.text: Great campground with lots to do close by and easier access to Paradise. Facilities are alright - need a bit of TLC, but nice to have flushing toilets and proper dish cleaning area. While we were surprised there wasn't a fire ban, you can no longer buy firewood at the campground and need to buy at Longmire for $15!! Seems a bit steep when it's typically $5 elsewhere...

reviews.author: Davide B.
reviews.text: Weel maintained, clean and quiet.

reviews.author: Brian D.
reviews.text: Nice, spacious, private sites with views of Mt. Rainier from campground.  Great trail to Carter Falls just across the street from the entrance.   Only one-half hour from Paradise Visitors' Center where there are many scenic trails to overlooks and waterfalls.  Beautiful area!

reviews.author: John S.
reviews.text: Availability Alert system works well. Happy to get a spot on short notice. Spaces are a bit tight. ‘Campground Full’ sign frustrating when there were sites empty the whole time we were there.

reviews.author: Dave  C.
reviews.text: Nice campground.  It would be great to have the firewood vendor on site like it was years ago.

reviews.author: Dave H.
reviews.text: This is always a family favorite spot. Good central location, sites are well maintained and bathrooms were clean. We went mid-week so it wasn’t too busy. Campers were all very nice as well as the camp hosts.

reviews.author: Jeff K.
reviews.text:
Campsite E19. Right by the road, lots of car noise all day. This campsite is easily 1/3 the size of other sites in the campground. It is a vehicle only site, and when you pull in, your car is 3 feet from the firepit, not ideal. We had room for a 10x10 pop up behind the van, also dangerously close to the fire pit due to the small campsite. And uneven behind the parking area. Trees limit the use of any other space on the site. Claims 2 parking spaces, there is no way you can fit 2 vehicles there. 
If you book at cougar rock, do not choose site E19.

reviews.author: Thomas H.
reviews.text: Great location with a helpful staff. Site D008 had a great pull through space for an RV if you have it and can comfortably also fit a tent

reviews.author: Marvin D.
reviews.text: Dirtiest bathroom I've ever seen.  Strong smell of ammonia. No dump station, no water hose connection to fill up my RV water tank, no electric connection, no showers.  Unfortunately, this is typical of US national parks.  I just came from Canada where they're much better.  They clean bathrooms daily, have hose connections, most have dump stations, showers and electric connections. The people at the help station were great.

reviews.author: Brian C.
reviews.text:
Another party on our campsite when we arrived at 7pm, and they initially refused to leave.  They had 3 excuses for why they should be there:
1.  "They" told us this was our spot for 2nd night.
2.  We heard there was a glitch in computer system.  Lots of people are double-booked.
3.  Our reservation shows we have tonight too.  I asked to see their booking, they declined.

Major hassle, and the 2 staff that checked me in were nowhere to be found at 7pm.  Major hassle that got became contentious.  My initials were on the campsite post slip, so they finally left after about an hour.  Kind of ruined our hiking/camping plans for that evening.

reviews.author: Mia W.
reviews.text: Beautiful site, plenty of privacy in the seating area in the woods, super walkable to a beautiful viewpoint and multiple waterfalls hikes.

reviews.author: Rafael L.
reviews.text: Very clean and organized campground. I loved the ranger programs and the presentation about glaciers!!

reviews.author: Lois B.
reviews.text: We were very glad to get a spot since they fill up quickly. We reserved a spot in the morning for that evening

reviews.author: Karen L.
reviews.text: Nice campground. Big area for tents. Clean facilities. You are near the road to the group campground but I didn’t find this disruptive at all as very few cars went down it. Loop E in general was quiet and enjoyable.

reviews.author: Robert E.
reviews.text: The campground was great.  The ranger registering me was friendly and efficient,  The campsite was great.  The bathrooms were clean and worked well.  I enjoyed a walk around the site.  It was beautiful with large trees and forest.

Basically, a well functioning campground. Facilities were in place and operating well, personnel coped well with the pressure of many visitors, and we got in, slept, used the toilets, and got out without mishap. The only downsides were relative: other campsites at MRNP had majestic trees, and a beautiful river (missing at cougar falls, AND, many of the campsites were closed due to 'tree hazards'. Maybe this is a short-term problem. I hope so. But it's strange that in the high season, so many sites aren't being used because a team with chainsaws aren't able to fix dead branches.

reviews.author: Jacob H.
reviews.text: What a great campsite!  Quiet and calm, large and private sites for tent camping, nice bathrooms, easy access to the park.  Would return!

reviews.author: Dale D.
reviews.text: The rangers and volunteers were very helpful.

reviews.author: Helen P.
reviews.text: Bare bones camp sites. Our site was spacious and quiet, but with a lot of dry debris and clean up needed, we were not comfortable having a campfire, and don’t understand why they are even allowed. Nice access to Longmire and Paradise. Was able to reserve a site in advance so was nice knowing we had a place to stay for the night and didn’t have to hurry for a first come first serve site.

reviews.author: Mehjabin M.
reviews.text: The tent pad was very uneven that our sleeping pad was continuously sliding in one direction. This is our second time camping at Couger rock campground. The toilets were not cleaned compared to our first visit

reviews.author: Raymond B.
reviews.text: Great camping location inside the park. Multiple waterfalls and lakes nearby, both driving and hiking. Just 2 miles to Longmire (ranger station, simple grocery items, small restaurant) and access to the Wonderland Trail is just .1 miles away.

reviews.author: Anna K.
reviews.text:
This campground is not for the rest.
We stayed here before climbing Rainier. We spent around 9 nights there. Place B10 is terrible:
1) it has garbage right on the place, people are terrible they make noise with recycling waste all night. Every single person thinks it’s great idea to throw the trash right before they go to restrooms before night. But we tried to sleep during these times.
2) noise from men’s restroom, I don’t know why this is so hard to close the door
3) lights from the restroom 
4) the food box at terrible place, it has sun all day long.
5) the place for tent has crazy angle, same as table
6) some of the people staying there just don’t know what camping is. They very loud, like I said after at late night they going to garbage with all their empty beer cans, they slam doors whole night at their cars. So bad

I don’t really understand why they need so many garbage bins at the campground around sites. Why just not have them at the exit 

Also people trying to get at their homes to loop B, is it not supposed to be just tent loop? 

This campground need the better host to keep quiet hours quite and better rules maybe mention that it’s not necessary to slam doors at 2 am like every 2 seconds for 15 minutes and trash. No trash at quiet hours

reviews.author: Cara D.
reviews.text: Our trip to Mt. Rainier National Park was exceptional! Our family enjoyed hiking and exploring, and the campground was an excellent way to unwind after a day of adventure. We will return!

reviews.author: Jeff T.
reviews.text: We were lucky enough to get the last first come site on a Saturday.  It was our first visit to the campground.  It was clean with spacious well cared for spaces.  The rangers and volunteers were very friendly and helpful.  We will be back!

reviews.author: John Austin B.
reviews.text:
Campground was well latex out with convenient access to bathrooms and waste/recycling no matter your location.  Quiet time was like someone flicked a switch - it was very quiet at night.  There were few bothersome wildlife, save some chipmunks and begging jays.  Sites varied, the first site was private and the second one my table and fire pit were 5’ from te road.  Thankfully very little traffic.  
1. A good jump off point for Paradise hikes and visiting the Nesquale riverbed.  Recommend dipping your feet in the glacial melt.  Firewood is small and insanely pricey, so I recommend buying 
Nearby outside the park.  Don’t try to get in the park on a Saturday morning - there will be a 45 minute bumper to bumper wait. Try Monday instead.

reviews.author: David K.
reviews.text: Site was reserved and ready for our arrival.  Site was reasonably level and had adequate privacy.  If you go to Paradise, and you should, go early like 0730-0800 early parking fills up really fast.  Wonderful hikes start in Paradise.

reviews.author: Alexander P.
reviews.text: A beautiful campground, well-located for access to some of the most popular hikes in the park.

reviews.author: David R.
reviews.text: Great location to stay! Had everything I needed!

reviews.author: Samantha  M.
reviews.text: Our site was close to the restrooms trash and water station and gave us an opportunity to do some night photography early in the morning and had the park to ourselves. Our site felt secluded even though we were close to others. Easy check in and easy to follow loops.

reviews.author: Jennifer L.
reviews.text:
Campground is very pretty, but be prepared for very small spots and small parking areas.  You really want to do your homework and check out sites online before choosing.  Some sites even have the table / fire and tent pad on different levels.

Also be aware that each loop only has one bathroom and one water spicket (located at the bathroom).  For us, this was a very long walk to retrieve water and bring it back to our site.  You will definitely water to bring some sort of water collection jug that you can drive or roll back to your site. 

You also need to plan ahead for firewood.  It is not sold at the campground, but at the general store about two miles away.  It would have been nice to know this before we arrived. 

Finally, I booked my reservation exactly six months in advance and received multiple confirmation reminders before my reservation.  However, about five hours before check in, I received an email that had a different site number.  When I arrived at the campground, the rangers couldn't figure out why I had been removed from my original site.  The one I was moved to was far smaller and couldn't accommodate four people.  I was eventually able to get my original site back, but only after multiple conversations with the rangers.

reviews.author: Kenza O.
reviews.text: Campsites were extremely well taken care of, the park rangers were extremely helpful and even gave alternative places to check out due to the high demand for this place.

reviews.author: Mike T.
reviews.text: Sites are very tight and best suited to smaller backpacking tents. It's still a very unique campground and very beautiful.

reviews.author: Mark C.
reviews.text: It's my ideal campground, quiet, deep in the forest. Short walk to the bathrooms. Lacking much sunlight, so dark (good for sleeping, but cold). No coverage for T-Mobile and no power hookup at sites.

reviews.author: Bill G.
reviews.text: Booked at a first come site at Cougar Rock Campground without any problem. Site was clean and comfortable. Rangers were always present and accommodating. Restroom was clean. Spent 4 days there while doing a series of challenging day hikes. Great base camp for exploring the park. Only downside was having Stevens Canyon Rd closed which limited access to the other side of the mtn. That was really a quality problem because there was plenty to do on the Longmire side.

reviews.author: Francois G.
reviews.text: Site not very large. Restroom clean. Beautiful place to stay

reviews.author: Josh B.
reviews.text:
Pros:
Nice campground. Everyone was respectful and loop C has a host living on it. Bathrooms were cleaned thoroughly ever day.

Cons:
As of summer 2023 a tree has been cut up and encroaching on the useable tent surface. A 7x9 tent fit but it was a bit tight. The site sits very close to another site and in close proximity to the bathroom. So you will get some light and noise coming from the bathroom doors, which started around 5am when we were there.

reviews.author: Mark L.
reviews.text: Real close to a trail that takes you to the nearby visitor center and branches off into other great trails. Clean bathrooms. Nice quiet campground.

reviews.author: Meaghan P.
reviews.text: We stayed at Cougar Rock for two nights with our toddler. The first night (campsite D11) we ended up next to some very noisy RV campers (cooking meals at 11 PM, elementary-aged children yelling, and headlamps flashing at our tent until after midnight). We spoke with Josh at the Ranger Station and he was so kind and moved us to a more secluded campsite. The next night was perfect-quiet and private. Would definitely stay here again if we could snag a more private campsite!

reviews.author: Shannon W.
reviews.text: The campground is kept very clean, including the bathrooms. Our site had numerous dead/fallen trees, which seemed like a fire hazard. The staff at check-in were very nice & helpful.

reviews.author: Walter M.
reviews.text: Well kept campsite with nearby water and flush toilets.  The tent area was very good.  Almost new picnic table.  Quick and easy check in.  Paradise was almost an hour up the road from the campsite.

reviews.author: STEVE M.
reviews.text: Excellent ranger support - and a very well run camp!

reviews.author: Aissata C.
reviews.text: I love that campground. There is stargazing at the Paradise visitor center and it is absolutely amazing. We did two hikes that were close to the campground and had a great experience with nature. I highly recommend this campground.

reviews.author: Sara W.
reviews.text: Campsite was clean and fairly private. It was on a corner and could be a little hard to pull into if you had a larger vehicle. Bathrooms were kept up and a short walk from campsite. Good location.

reviews.author: NOELL D.
reviews.text: This campground is very well maintained and in a great location surrounded by, or not far from, hiking trails. The sites are clean and somewhat secluded from your neighbor. It's about a 20min drive to Paradise, which has all the Mount Rainier accessible trails and full wifi. I'd definitely stay here, again!

reviews.author: Larry S.
reviews.text: We loved the campsite and campground.  It was quiet and amazing

reviews.author: David M.
reviews.text: Nice site and close to the bathroom and wTer

reviews.author: John M.
reviews.text: I enjoyed being under all the big trees.

reviews.author: Earl C.
reviews.text: Awesome place, paper towel in the restroom always refilled, campground host always patrolling the area which was great. Carter falls trailhead just yards away from the main campground entrance and it was nice to hangout next to the river around 6 pm when no one around

reviews.author: Jim B.
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed three nights on B-Loop and it was very peaceful. Bathrooms had flush toilets--nice. A bit of a walk to them. Will pick one closer next time. Big complaint-- firewood cannot be purchased at the campground!! The shed was full of firewood and ranger said they just store it there....huh? He couldn't understand either. You have to buy it before entering park or go to Longmire store to buy for $13.80 + tax per bundle!!! And the bundles were smallish. I spent $60 for four bundles--outrageous. Why doesn't park management address this issue and try to help campers? I could afford it but many can't. The staff should try to HELP campers, not make it difficult. Just don't understand....
Cougar Rock is close to several nice hiking trails, including Carter Falls, Comet Falls and parts of Wonderland Trail.

reviews.author: Cindy H.
reviews.text: Arrived with a group needing 3 campsites and did not have a reservation. The ranger was fantastic finding sites that accommodated our tent sizes and were close together. The sites were perfect, the weather was fantastic as always, and we had a great time.

reviews.author: Earl C.
reviews.text: Great campsite

reviews.author: John P.
reviews.text: The campsite is pretty small. It barely fit my 3man tent. If you have a bigger tent, it would definitely not fit - at least in my site.

reviews.author: Skylar W.
reviews.text: lovely foresty campground on the southwest side of the park! we were able to snag a spot via rec.gov the night prior. our spot (D36) was a bit small, but fit our 19ft van (any bigger would have been tight) and we were able to string up a hammock. we walked around all the loops with our dog, it’s a huge campground with many lovely spots, ranging all different sizes. first come first serve might have provided us a cooler spot, but we were a cross from the clean bathrooms, there is potable water available, and it was quiet, so we can’t complain!

reviews.author: DHRUV P.
reviews.text:
Had RV, and dumping station was closed.
But other than that, everything was pretty normal as any other campground.

reviews.author: Brigid Q.
reviews.text: It was a very well maintained campground in a convenient location and made for a very comfortable stay,

reviews.author: Ken D.
reviews.text: Hot & dry, pray for rain. Lot’s of maintenance backlog, numerous sites are closed due to hazard trees needing to be removed. Limited staff, bathrooms ok but the one in A/B loop was always overly busy, I think the one on the next loop over may have been out of service. Interaction with NPS staff always positive but hey, let’s get this park some money to take care of the place! This is America’s 5th oldest NP.

reviews.author: Elisabeth R.
reviews.text: Very nice site - on the larger side. We had a 4-person tent and it was easy to set up in the space. Wished we had brought our hammock, plenty of trees to hold it.  Fire pit but no bear-box for food storage.  We had to cross another site to go to the bathroom a bit downhill.  Garbage boxes near the bathroom but away enough from site.  easy enough as the site was not occupied.  no mosquitoes on the 4th of July weekend.  beautiful hikes around.  Will be back.

reviews.author: Tess C.
reviews.text: Went late June, the campground was clean and quiet. No issues with check in

reviews.author: Keith E.
reviews.text: Very nice, although trail access is somewhat limited (really only two options).

reviews.author: Rosemary V.
reviews.text: Would have enjoyed the experience more if generator use had been enforced. Several campsites near us, B17, ran generators during non-generator hours for long periods of time.

reviews.author: Katherine H.
reviews.text: Great campground with nice, nook-like forest campsites among the boulders making the camping experience feel more private than typical in national park campgrounds. Excellent walking access to the Wonderland Trail and Nisqually River flowing from the Nisqually Glacier. Will definitely return!

reviews.author: Tami H.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Big and private sites. Easy walk to restrooms. Great view of Mount Rainier across the road. Loved staying here.

reviews.author: V M.
reviews.text: We loved the campground. We had site D12. It was a quite difficult to get the motorhome level. I thibk there are other numbers that are leveler. We have a 29’ and it fit well. The campsite is near the river with view on the mountain.  Too bad the dump is closed this year. No cell phone reception whatsoever not for Verizon/Tmobile and non for AT&T

reviews.author: Richard W.
reviews.text: Delightful staff. Clean camp sites. Beautiful surroundings. A+

reviews.author: Kirk R.
reviews.text: Campground was clean, private and ready. It was in of the most beautiful forests I have ever seen. We loved our experience. Restrooms were clean and well cared for. Thank you Rainier NPS!

reviews.author: Matthew H.
reviews.text: Such an amazing stay. Loved it all the way!

reviews.author: Elisa J.
reviews.text: We stayed one night in a tent and we were very comfortable. We wouldn't hesitate to return!

reviews.author: Michael P.
reviews.text: Easy check-in at the site. Friendly and helpful person who checked me in.

reviews.author: Jeremy F.
reviews.text:
We stayed at B029 in a large tent and it wasn’t bad. We didn’t think that RV sites usually meant uneven terrain but we lucked out. We were able to put up a 10-person tent, park my Highlander next to it, park our 4Runner with batwing awning, and a bathroom shower tent between them all on the RV pad. We then had lots of ground space for the campsite activities and kitchen setup. Bear box on site with picnic table and decent fire ring. Fire ring has a clam style grate that can sit over or fold backward away. 

This is our second time at Cougar rock this 2023 season and they definitely need to clean up their forest. So many dead or dying trees need to be felled. We had small twigs and branches fall while we were there for 2 nights. Nobody was hit but it is clear there are hazards, hence the 4-star. Site gets partial sunlight that rotates around the trees so using our solar panel for our Jackery worked even though we had to chase the Sun spots throughout the day.

reviews.author: Garland W.
reviews.text: Great campgrounds. Clean, and well maintained sites. Water fountains were not working. Other than that was a great stay.

reviews.author: Steven K.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite in a great location!

reviews.author: Janet H.
reviews.text: Great location, trail near campground.

reviews.author: Janet H.
reviews.text: Good location, a bit crowded.

reviews.author: Janelle W.
reviews.text: I loved everything but the neighbor's rooster. Not much i could do about it, Big spots, hiking trail right there, easy access to Rainier. I will be back, thank you!

reviews.author: Steve B.
reviews.text: Ranger picked out a great available spot for my 20 foot van, nice and level.

reviews.author: Glenda J C.
reviews.text: Newly cut down dead trees stacked every where. The cutting went on during the day. Few sites open due to hazardous trees. Site selection made by on site ranger, not your choice.

reviews.author: Jo K.
reviews.text: The museum was closed at the time but we had so much fun walking the trails and eating by the fire. Every worker we encountered and asked questions were very informative and helpful! Can’t wait to go back! We stayed in loop c across from the bathrooms and water. Very helpful when my kids have little bladders!

reviews.author: Michael H.
reviews.text:
We loved this campground and really appreciated the "pull-though" drive.  We found it to be very quiet and, on the days we were there, not crowded.  The Ranger talk was fun too.
Can't wait to return to Mr. Rainier National Park - and Cougar Rock.

reviews.author: Nichole T.
reviews.text: Best site in the campground I think - private and shaded

reviews.author: Donald W.
reviews.text: Great views and good bathrooms

reviews.author: Michelle D.
reviews.text: Such a great place to camp to be able to do so much hiking. The campground is very nice and quiet.

reviews.author: Cory V.
reviews.text: Staff was friendly and courteous.  Not many generators or giant diesel haulers.  Relatively peaceful

reviews.author: George B.
reviews.text:
We were in Loop A during the last week of the season. It's such a beautiful campground with spacious sites and easy access to the Longmire and Paradise. There were lots of other tenters which gave it an old-time feel. 
Nice rangers and volunteers.

reviews.author: Loan L.
reviews.text: Overall, excellent service, very spacious, very quiet and private. The ranger at check-in was also vey pleasant and helpful in providing recommendations for specific lots. I liked that there were communal food storage, restrooms, water foundations, and recycling/trash.

reviews.author: Russ P.
reviews.text: The campground and facilities are great - clean bathrooms, friendly staff, and wide variety of sites available.  Easy access to some great hiking and beautiful scenery.  Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Yvonne S.
reviews.text: Nice site, no showers. very quiet and staff were very friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: Connor H.
reviews.text: Gorgeous hikes and views all around. No phone service but that was a blessing to really get away from it all. Ended up extending for an 8 day stay.

reviews.author: kathleen G.
reviews.text:
Nice campground in a world-class national park:
We had a little trepidation about traveling to a very popular national park while the camping was first-come, first-serve only.  But as it is at the end of the season, it was reasonable to expect some vacancies.  And indeed, there were enough spots to choose from.  Some sites were a little close to others, which made ours seem less personal.  And because of a warm spell, the campground did in fact fill to capacity.
But the restrooms were clean, the grounds were well-maintained.  The only issues were a huge tree that had fallen into one of the campsites, making it unusable.  And our own site had experienced a washout on the exit portion of the pull-through.  In order not to have to back out with a trailer, I had to do a little road building to fill in enough to get my car up and out.
But this is the third time I have camped at Mt. Rainier national park, and it will not be the last.

reviews.author: sheila k.
reviews.text:
We stayed 3 nights.  The 1st afternoon, a rented RV pulled into the site across from us. There were about 6 adults who clearly were drinking on the way to RNP. They played music for hours and continued to drink.  Not enjoyable.
The 2nd afternoon, 2 male adults pulled into the same site.  They too were drinking and continued to. We kept hearing the clanking of metal and discovered one of them was using a throwing ax and hitting/lodging it into a large douglas fir trunk with it.  Repeatedly. For hours. The 3rd night most of the loop was empty - and quiet.

reviews.author: Kathryn G.
reviews.text: Great access to Rainier lovely campground.

reviews.author: Laura L.
reviews.text:
Cougar Rock is what I would call a traditional National Park campground. Clean restrooms with fresh water and waste water dumping, neat sites with gorgeous old growth forest, all situated close to popular park attractions. We stayed in the no generator loop which made for a peaceful experience. 
I would come back in a heartbeat!!

reviews.author: Matthew S.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with unique sites and decent spacing. Didn’t have any issues with noise. Very close to Nisqually River and cool viewpoints there. All staff I spoke with were very kind and helpful. Make sure you buy firewood in Ashford before getting to the park, they charge $15/bundle (small bundles) at the national park store. Washroom facilities were clean but could certainly use some updating. I didn’t find anywhere in this area of the park that was suitable for bathing/rinsing off (showers, lakes, rivers, etc.). I went on a weekday in late September and had no issue getting a first come/first serve site when I showed up around 2:30 pm. All in all I very much enjoyed my stay and wish I could have stayed longer!

reviews.author: Enrique R.
reviews.text: N/A

reviews.author: Hsien C.
reviews.text: The camp ground is run by the Mount Rainer National Park ranger and the campsite site fee is collected by the ranger at the entrance to the campsite. It's a first come first serve campsite, but they never advice you that you can book one night at a time and extend the stay the next morning. And they never advice me that if you book more than one day the first day, it not refundable if next morning you decided not to stay the 2nd night. There isn't any policy regarding to booking anywhere at the campsite ranger station. Also they advice you  if you have military pass, senior pass or access pass which give you 50% discount for the campsite. They just charge you the regular campsite fee regardless.

reviews.author: Holly B.
reviews.text: Pleasant wooded sites, clean restrooms.

reviews.author: Jeannie C.
reviews.text: Stayed here for two nights in September at E loop.  Great campground had a nice view of Mt Rainier in the morning. It’s a first come first serve but it fills out quickly.  Best to stop at the ranger booth before you drive in to find a spot chances are it might have been reserved prior. I will camp here again.

reviews.author: Morgan S.
reviews.text: Rolling in just before dark and never having been at the campground before the rangers on duty were informative, welcoming, and extremely kind.  The campground's tree density really cut down on the sound of families more than I'd expected, which was great!  As an overnight before heading up some of the Paradise hikes first thing in the morning I know I'll be back.

reviews.author: Paul H.
reviews.text: Nice campground, good price. Wish they'd fix dump, or at least fresh water. Come on now!

reviews.author: Andrew F.
reviews.text: Friendly and helpful staff. Check in process was a relative breeze. Campground is quiet, with plenty of good size pitches. All the basic facilities you need for camping are provided. Location is ideal for exploring the south side of Mt Rainier. Recommended.

reviews.author: Glenna B.
reviews.text: We spent 3 nights in 3rd week of September mid week.  Beautiful weather!  Wonderful park service staff finding us a spot we would fit in.  Check in at the check in station (the sign directs you to do so) and they will help you out so you aren’t driving around to find a spot that works. They know what you will fit into!   Great place to camp.  Just a few miles to Paradise.  And Longmeyer is right down the road.  Great mid point to camp and then to explore the park during the daytime. Absolutely gorgeous park and a wonderful camp area!

reviews.author: Theresa G.
reviews.text: Better bring your cell phone and credit card as no cash is accepted here any more.

reviews.author: Donna E.
reviews.text: Ranger was courteous and helpful.  Sites were well kept and the price is reasonable.  Bathrooms had flush toilets and warm water in the sinks, and there was a place to wash cookware and dishes.    Wonderful view of Mt. Rainier.  BUT. Bring big your own firewood.  Purchasing firewood at Longmire is not a good idea!!

reviews.author: BRIAN S.
reviews.text: We're into the first come, first served season, with closed loops. I knew from the website that A and B loops were open, but I didn't know that E loop was open -- or that E loop is no-generator. I detest generators, so it would have been useful to know this ahead of time. I didn't find it out until after I had chosen a site in A loop.

reviews.author: Troy S.
reviews.text: Easy booking. Clean campground.

reviews.author: Holly B.
reviews.text:
Campsite was fairly private, neighbors were respectful of quiet hours. Ranger talk on nite sounds was fun and I actually recognized a spotted owl a few nights later due to her talk!  Also, those chirping “birds” at dusk are really bats. With my senior access pass a tent sight was just $10. A real deal. Restrooms clean, trash can area picked up, bear box at each site. 

This campground was a nice option I stumbled into and would recommend.

reviews.author: John S.
reviews.text: Great base for hiking around the Park including a trail to Longmire Museum from where you can hike a number of more and less strenuous trails

reviews.author: Ryan B.
reviews.text: No cell service, but great campsite

reviews.author: Julia W.
reviews.text: Great well run campground!

reviews.author: Jim N.
reviews.text: Had an excellent spot.  The campground was full, but didn't feel that way to us!

reviews.author: George O.
reviews.text: A lot of unlevel spots

reviews.author: Kylie D.
reviews.text: Went at the start of the off-season, had to walk a bit to the restrooms from the site due to various loop closures from tree damage/closing for the season. Be sure to check on fires, closures, etc when visiting any NP! The staff were friendly and helpful with planning around the fire below the park and accomplishing seeing what we could with the smoke.

reviews.author: John L.
reviews.text:
The campground was outrageously beautiful.  The sites were spacious and well spaced.  The staff was super helpful.
What was not good was the website to reserve.  We tried to call to get more info but we’re unable to find a number to get answers.  After Labor Day we understood we could not reserve a site.  On the list sites some were blank, some were ff meaning first come first serve.  Yet some sites were R for reserved in the middle of fr on either side.  It made no sense.  We arrived at 11am on a Wednesday thinking that would be safe.  But on that day the park service decided to close three loops.  50 campers lined up at 6 am to try to move to open loops.  The next day a loop was reopened.  We felt it was bad communication on the website and why close loops so early with so many anxious to camp?

Once we got a site on Thursday the experience was great.

reviews.author: Loyd O.
reviews.text:
The staff was amazing working to move our reservation around to accommodate our limited backcountry permits.  We did have to move our site right off, but did not have to come out of the backcountry just to move mid stay.
   The bathrooms were well maintained.  Water and the dump station would have been a huge plus, but it was closed for maintenance I assume.
  Our only criticism is that many to most of the RV lots are not very level.  We had 7 inch disparity in the site A013 from side to side.  It was very difficult to level and we still had a slope with all our leveling gear employed. Not sure if the sites could be graded a bit, but that would really improve the site for RVs.

reviews.author: Samantha R.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite. Easy to access restrooms, and tons of recreational opportunities nearby.

reviews.author: Al T.
reviews.text:
Nice campground.  Very quiet.
Close to the visitor center.
Excellent staff.

reviews.author: Matthew G.
reviews.text: Be aware that after labor day couger rock campground closes loops. If you have a reservation on Labor day in loops B,C, or D and want to stay another day - they close those loops the next day and you will have to move. To move you will have to battle about 30 other campers and get in line at 6am the next day to get a site as they move everyone into A, E, and R loops.

reviews.author: Jong H.
reviews.text: The campsite is clean and at a convenient location. There is no water and no electricity at the site but public restrooms are available in the campgrounds. There is no shower though. There were quite a few mosquitos at the sit at dusk.

reviews.author: Delaney K.
reviews.text: The rangers at the campground were super nice and helpful! The facilities were clean and the campsite was private and cozy. The only bummer was how long it took to get into the park both times (first to enter via Nisqually then back through White River) but while in the park things were smooth sailing. The Henry Jackson Visitor Center had a lot of easy hikes and great views and would recommend checking it out!

reviews.author: Shaunna B.
reviews.text:
I love the Cougar campground! I’ve been there 3 times this year.  It was relaxing and so enjoyable! The campground has restrooms and potable water. It does not have showers.
The campsites are clean and most are spacious. The rangers and volunteers are awesome, and I give my experiences a big 10 out of 10!

reviews.author: Megan W.
reviews.text: Nice campsite, good access to the Paradise area. Bathrooms fairly clean (no showers, but you can take a bird bath in the sink). They didn't have as many water stations as expected, so make sure you bring a bucket or a gallon-sized water jug to port your water to and from your campsite.

reviews.author: Donald W.
reviews.text: Great location. Sites are generous sizes. Rangers are pleasant too

reviews.author: Betsie D.
reviews.text: Campground was very quiet. I'd like to see fewer campfires when there's no need for the warmth, as was the case during our stay.  Seems a waste of energy and adds to poor air quality.  We enjoyed the ranger talk in the evening.  Be sure to check out the bulletin boards.

reviews.author: Lisa  S.
reviews.text: Being close to mount Ranier was the best part. The campground was peaceful and clean.

reviews.author: Chaojun L.
reviews.text: great campsite.  our site is a pull through site, easy for RV parking.  restroom is very clean. 15 min drive to Paradise visitor center.

reviews.author: Gillian V.
reviews.text: Lots of trees, shade, greenspace and no mosquitoes, blackflies or other bitey things. Nice and quiet, good recycling, picnic table and firepit in top condition - the only limitation is no showers... had to go for a swim in Bench lake instead :)

reviews.author: Richard C.
reviews.text: We arrived at about noon on a Monday in late August and were able to get a campsite.  The ranger at the check in was able to match our site to the type of tent we were camping in.  We had an excellent site and were very pleased with our stay.

reviews.author: Colleen G.
reviews.text: Campsites very open and close together - ours was very close to the road.  Great location for Mt. Rainier/Longmire activities and hiking.

reviews.author: Shambhavi B.
reviews.text: Great campground inside the park. Clean restrooms, close to Paradise and Longmire and hiking trails.

reviews.author: alysha f.
reviews.text: Great experience. Just watch out for falling pine cones hitting your tent, car etc. squirrels pick them whenever they want. My windshield got a couple of small chips from squirrels picking pine cones at 6am! It sucks but I can't be mad at that, it's their home and how they eat. Just warning others to try not to park close the trees.

reviews.author: Dave M.
reviews.text: The only negative I have to say is the lack of firewood for sale at the campsite.  While other campgrounds within the park either have bundles available for sale or a truck that makes rounds and sells bundles, campers at CR can only look at the bundles reserved for Rainier Guest Services, or else be directed to Ashford, outside the park to get some.  It would be great if fire wood was available for campers here - it would keep them from scavenging the various branches from nearby trees.

reviews.author: Hardik M.
reviews.text: Very near to Mt. Rainier, enjoyed the evening ranger talk at the campground amphitheater.

reviews.author: james h.
reviews.text: Mount Ranier is our favorite National Park and Cougar Rock campground makes our stay so enjoyable! Only downside is that the dump station and potable water station have been shut down for the past 2 years! Makes RV life difficult

reviews.author: Nicole B.
reviews.text: I would have said excellent, I didn’t notice the fifth star. It’s a beautiful campground and quiet!

reviews.author: Brianna R.
reviews.text: Great campsite. Clean, quiet, and near a water station / bathroom.

reviews.author: Sai Hemantha Chowdary P.
reviews.text:
The campground is pretty neat and well maintained. The dump stations and bathrooms are good enough. The metal storage boxes are an added safety amenity. Each campground is spacious and secluded. There are also several first come first serve sites.
On one of the nights we attended a great presentation in the Amphitheater by one of the Rangers about the Nisqually River and it’s history which was really interesting and informative.

reviews.author: Partricia Y.
reviews.text: What's not to like?

reviews.author: Evan  S.
reviews.text: Great campsite in close proximity to paradise. Extending your stay by one night is usually possible but you have to get up at 630 am and get in line at the ranger station. Running water, clean bathrooms, good trash system. Definitely more populated than white river.

reviews.author: Malia M.
reviews.text: Clean camp spots & bathrooms with running water. Bonus!

reviews.author: Angelo B.
reviews.text: Excellent campground and by far one of my favorites. This site was super private, but the site behind was a little bit close. I didn’t mind though as the people were very quiet and respectful. The site was well thought out and it was really quiet and pitch black by 10pm which was nice! Would definitely stay at this site again.

reviews.author: Neilson N.
reviews.text: We missed our reserved night because of logistics. The next day we arrive at Rainier and I visit this campground for first come first serve camping. There were 12 sites at that time on my phone still available..."ranger" said there were zero available..I walked in and those same spots were empty...not a coincidence. Maybe it was close to the end of the workers shift? I don't understand and I think it's pathetic.

reviews.author: Jason B.
reviews.text: Good

reviews.author: Brendon S.
reviews.text: Rangers we’re great, Rainer is great. The site A8 is incredibly noisy 27/7 as it backs to the main road. The site was the dustiest I’ve ever been in. It was like they were emptying the fire pits by spreading ash throughout the site.  The restrooms were very clean.

reviews.author: RICHARD F.
reviews.text: Loved the rustic setting, lectures at the amphitheater and the friendly staff

reviews.author: Christa S.
reviews.text: My husband and I had the best weekend getaway at Rainier! This campground is a prime location, and we hope to make this an annual summer tradition.✨

reviews.author: Raechel D.
reviews.text: We had a great time and will be back again one day!

reviews.author: Jennifer L.
reviews.text: Love this camp ground. The amenities are very nice (clean bathrooms, potable water, big garbage bins that don’t overflow), friendly rangers. But the best part is this campground is the ranger program. I am a 39 year old woman who only recently got into nature-y things. But I am just as excited as any kid to listen to the ranger teaching us about the glaciers. Thank you for this great campground and thank you to the park rangers that work hard to maintain this place!

reviews.author: yoji y.
reviews.text: You can see Mt.Rainier from the campsite. It is located inside the entrance, so you don’t need to be in line the gate.

reviews.author: Brian C.
reviews.text: We had an awesome site and it was a very peaceful campground. It was very smoky since the canopy holds the campfire smoke in but then again you get to have a campfire!

reviews.author: Tricia B.
reviews.text: So nice to have campgrounds like this in NPs, especially with helpful amd friendly Rangers.

reviews.author: Vicki M.
reviews.text:
The campground was outstanding!  The sites were clean and private, and had everything we needed.  My husband and I were camping with four of our 8-10 year old grandchildren and enjoyed our time immensely.  The bathrooms were clean and close to each campsite.

There were two reasons I didn't give this a 5-star rating.  1. The woman who registered us talked about her college degree, her experiences in college, and her work history with the man who was registering in front of us. She talked incessantly while we stood in line and our children waited in the car. 2. The amphitheater was scheduled to have a talk about nocturnal animals.  We talked with the kids and pumped them up for the ranger.  Unfortunately, the talk was about the solar system and well over the heads of our kids.   Other than those two things, it was a 5 star experience.

reviews.author: Julie H.
reviews.text: Lovely experience at Cougar Rock for our first time there. We particularly love the ranger programs and our kids (7 and 9) liked the amphitheater... they put on their own play and invited everyone to come see it :) . The bathroom path in loop B inexplicably runs right through another campsite (literally the middle of their driveway), which was a little awkward. Overall there isn't a lot of privacy between campsites but it was more "line of sight" other people rather than "everyone is on top of us," and that's what we expected to find at a popular campground. We enjoyed a four-night stay with hiking nearby and easy access to Paradise.

reviews.author: Debra S.
reviews.text: We had two side by side campsites (E15 and 16), big enough for three tents and 9 people.  Bathrooms super clean.  Checking in was really easy.  Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Carol S.
reviews.text:
Reservations mean nothing here!  We made our reservation months in advance, selecting a site near a restroom because a person in our party has a medical issue.  After checking in, we went to our reserved site only to find it occupied.  A tent and other items were there, but no people.  
We went back to the ranger station, waiting in line again, and the ranger didn't care at all.  His solution was for us to find another site.  After 45 minutes, we found another.  There were few empty sites and none near a restroom.  We returned to the ranger station, waiting in line again, to find that the dude had no recollection of our conversation and situation. 

Well, we stayed 1 night. It wasn't great as the site wasn't right for us.  We noticed that the squatters returned to our reserved site and stayed there likely for free.  No one came around to check reservations. So, you make reservations months in advance. Drive the long drive to get there, wait 1.5 hours to enter the park, then find your supposedly reserved site taken and they don't do anything about it.

reviews.author: Cory L.
reviews.text: Very nice campground. We stayed in loop D which doesn’t have bear boxes at each site so just be prepared to leave food in your car. We will definitely be camping here again.

reviews.author: Ian O.
reviews.text: The campground and park employees were excellent. Grounds are well maintained, campers were all very nice and respectful. My only complaint is the reservation system for this campground. I tried to reserve a site online months in advance the day the sites became available to reserve. I tried to do this for several days but there was never a single site available no matter when I checked. How is that possible? I ended up taking a chance and got a first come first serve site. But what is the deal with the online reservations, how come I couldn’t see any open sites at all months in advance? Not even a single night midweek? Something seems wrong, should have asked some people with reservations what they did.

reviews.author: Jay S.
reviews.text: Nice campground conveniently located near the Longmire wilderness information center. Every time I stay there I get a nice site and people are generally quiet and respectful.

reviews.author: Kathleen B.
reviews.text: Quiet and lovely setting. Hazard trees were removed last year from many sites but that made viewing the night stars easier. The restroom was very clean and rangers at check-in friendly and informative.

reviews.author: Hua A.
reviews.text: Convinient location. Clean bathrooms. We got a first come first serve site on a Tuesday. Very happy with it.

reviews.author: Erin W.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground and close to the beach.

reviews.author: Roma C.
reviews.text: Great campsite #6. Even though it was a crowded campground there was privacy and well spaced spots. Nice trees and boulders through out.

reviews.author: BRIAN B.
reviews.text: It was a very nice campground and each site was unique.  My only advice to bring large containers of water to avoid multiple trips to the single water source near restroom. Nice and quiet and nice shade after a long day of hiking in the sun.  Can't wait to go back!  Also the flush toilets and bathrooms were very clean.

reviews.author: Steven P.
reviews.text: Campground is great. Good location. Nice sites.

reviews.author: Avinash A.
reviews.text: Very pleasant experience. The rangers were happy to help. Every campsite has ample shade. Hardly any insects / mosquitoes mid summer.

reviews.author: Lindsay L.
reviews.text: Pleasantly surprised by the privacy of this particular campsite

reviews.author: John O.
reviews.text:
Great location for RV campground close to Paradise & Longmire.  We spent 4 days and hiked to see many beautiful waterfalls with beautiful weather.  Mountain was visible every day.   Staffing in the area is an issue like everywhere else but they did a great job in town.  Example:  Gift shop in Paradise Inn was closed Tuesday & Wednesday due to staffing issues and dining at the Paradise Inn was limited.   Roads are narrow and winding thru the park... just have to take  your time.  
Many camping sites are not level so be prepared.   Camp rangers were very friendly and park was well taken care of.   We would definitely camp here again.  
There is ZERO cellular signal at the campground.   Nearest signal is in Paradise and limited spotty signal in Longmire.

reviews.author: Jacek W.
reviews.text: Shower addition would be great

reviews.author: Tracey W.
reviews.text: Great location and close proximity to a number of hiking trails! There are some campsites better that others. We had B 031 and the car parking spot was super uneven so we had to use blocks to even it out. There was a spot across from us that was reserved for several days but no one showed up until our last day. I wished we could have parked there as the driveway way super flat. It would bd great to know if a slot wasn’t going to be used. The cost us very reasonable so , I suspect the campsites reserved but unused were under utilized. I loved the experience though!!

reviews.author: Pieter L.
reviews.text:
Great place close to Mount Rainier!
We were lucky on getting a FF-site.
It was a little tilted but with a great fireplace. Bring your own firewood: is not for sale on the campgrounds and the nearest store is a rip-off.

To bad the dump station was out of order.

reviews.author: Ryan M.
reviews.text: Camping spot was nice and shaded and flat.  Would camp here again.

reviews.author: Lynne Y.
reviews.text: Mt Rainier wildflowers were spectacular.  We heard (but didnt see) the glaciers creaking and groaning.  Wonderful national park to visit!

reviews.author: Martin R.
reviews.text: A classic, old-time, national park campground in a mature forest with private, secluded sites.  Relaxing and quiet!

reviews.author: Paul S.
reviews.text: The site did not have a lot of privacy in the direction of the picnic table and firepit.  We were able to orient our vehicle in the other direction giving us a very private space over a forested small ravine.  The overall campground is huge and made for a great morning walk with the dog.

reviews.author: Scott C.
reviews.text: Cougar Rock Campground was an ideal place to explore Mt Rainier National Park. There is an easy -.5 mile hike to o Longmire and various trailheads and a short drive to Patadise and many more higher elevation trails, falls, and glaciers.

reviews.author: Dora L.
reviews.text: Close to Carter Falls trail. Sneak peek views of Mt. Rainier through the tree lines.

reviews.author: Benjamin Y.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with great sites and very close to carter falls

reviews.author: Kate S.
reviews.text: Pleasant, well tended camp site and bathrooms. Felt fairly private despite  the campground being full. Easy walk across Paradise Road to pick up the Wonderland Trail and get incredible views of the mountain and Paradise River. Would definitely camp here again!

reviews.author: Russ S.
reviews.text: My biggest reason for giving a 5 Star review is simply because there were National Park employees in the campground. Over the last several years I have seen this type of customer service erode to a total lack of presence in our National Parks. The ranger we spoke with filled us in on how to get a first come first serve site the following day. Simple info to pass along first hand, but almost impossible to find online. Also, props to the govt for hosting their own reservation service with no fees. Wish State Parks would do the same thing!

reviews.author: Kathleen A.
reviews.text: great campground

reviews.author: Maureen  j.
reviews.text:
Staff were extremely friendly 
Bathroom etc were very clean
Sites were well spaced

reviews.author: Alice L.
reviews.text: Amazing locale. Great staff.

reviews.author: Kelly B.
reviews.text: They assigned us this campsite and it was RIGHT next to R13. No WAY would we ever choose this site if we were given the choice. Camping with a friend? Awesome. Stranger? Awful.

reviews.author: Wendy B.
reviews.text: Loved the fire pit area surrounded by stars and trees slightly off to side from our RV.  Great to walk across road to Nisqually river - and up to Carter falls. Best tasting water we ever had also!

reviews.author: Kimberly W.
reviews.text: We were surprised to get a site in July at Mount Rainier but it was very nice, picnic area. Fire ring in good shape. The park ranger who signed us in was very nice.

reviews.author: Jaime C.
reviews.text: Frustrated that there was no dump site and not noted ahead of time and the bathrooms left a lot to be desired

reviews.author: Cindy Z.
reviews.text: We had a great time during our 2 nights stay at cougar rock campground, close to everything, spacious, lots of privacy.

reviews.author: Staci C.
reviews.text: Bathroom was clean. Staff was very nice. Came by to tell us about programs. Very nice stay.

reviews.author: Patricia  S.
reviews.text: Our campsite was fairly private and quiet. We had a picnic table, fire ring and bear box. They kept the bathroom clean. The whole area is so beautiful. I would definitely stay there again.

reviews.author: Mindy R.
reviews.text: We had a great trip!

reviews.author: Dennis L.
reviews.text: Very nice campground. Lots of sites but still feels very private as there are lots of trees between each site. It's nice to have a place to park an RV and a flat spot for a tent or a kitchen area. Nice bathrooms. Easy walk to trails and access to both paradise and Longmire. Only issue is firewood. They state that firewood should come from no more than 50 miles away which is completely understandable.  However the firewood avilable for sale at Longmire is $15 per bundle. They had one bundle available and it had 5 pieces in it. Small pieces....So each small piece of wood was $3. Yet, they are in the process of thining the diseased trees around the campground and there are hundreds of downed trees. Needless to say people have been taking wood from these. When you make something prohibitively expensive you encourage people to use other resources.

reviews.author: Alex P.
reviews.text: Exceptional campsite, in the middle of the dense forest. It has no bear box, so you have to put everything back in your car. No firewood for sale at the campground, the store in Longmire sells bundles at $15 each. Wildlife seen: 1 bunny. Great campground for hiking Panorama.

reviews.author: Tulsi P.
reviews.text:
My husband and I camped at site C15 and enjoyed our time there. It’s a partially shaded site at the end of the loop, so there’s decent privacy. This particular site is better for an RV/camper as it has a spacious pull through driveway. We were tent camping and could only find one small area that was level enough for our tent. We walked around the other loops and it seems Loop D has more sites with true tent pads. 

Bathrooms were well-maintained and clean. There is good garbage disposal and recycling for select items. Any staff we interacted with was very friendly. Location is great in terms up getting up to Paradise and other big sights. No cell reception for Verizon or T-Mobile, but we were able to get service by Paradise Inn.

Firewood is only sold at Longmire general store and it’s a bit pricey ($15 a bundle). I’d recommend buying firewood from somewhere nearby to get better bang for your buck.

reviews.author: kathleen d.
reviews.text: The campsite had no shade for most of the day. The ground was pretty level,  but rocky and hard to put stakes through. The proximity to the bathrooms was appreciated, not too close and not too far. It was a short distance to the Wonderland Trail, which made it convenient to make a day out of hiking to beautiful Carter Falls, Narada Falls and Reflection Lake. The rangers were friendly and helpful and I enjoyed their evening presentations. The lack of shade though was frustrating. Didn’t like coming to a hot tent after a long hike or trying to avoid the setting sun while I was making dinner on the table and bench.

reviews.author: Michael B.
reviews.text:
Lots of hazard trees down in the campground, waiting for disposal - barriers to restrooms.
D loop north restroom utility sink clogged and water spigot non-functional.

reviews.author: Emily D.
reviews.text: We so enjoyed our time here. Camp sites offered plenty of room. Bathrooms were clean with nice water refill station and kitchen sink. We enjoyed our morning walks through camp with the dogs and got to see Rainier from camp and the river. Great base camp to get to Paradise and Longmire. Even a nice enjoyable drive to Snow Lake trailhead.

reviews.author: Adriana D.
reviews.text: I loved staying at Cougar Rock! It was well located in the park, so I could get to all different areas I wanted to explore. The rangers were super helpful and the bathroom facilities were always clean and well stocked. I loved that you could walk across the street to the Carter Falls trail and sit by the river and enjoy a beautiful view of Mt. Rainier. Would happily stay there again!

reviews.author: Kyle L.
reviews.text: Nice campground. Be mindful of which site you choose because there aren’t paths through camping areas to bathrooms. You need to use the road.

reviews.author: Denise T.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsites in dense forest offers much privacy. The bathrooms were clean. The only down side was the firewood. It was nearly $15/bundle, which you have to buy down the road (not at the campground) and they ran out. In addition, the park has a no collecting of firewood rule within the park.

reviews.author: Biljana  P.
reviews.text: The campgrounds are beautiful. Park ranges are very tentative.

reviews.author: Charlie W.
reviews.text: Spent 2 nights at Cougar Rock. Campsite was clean and roomy - we three were in a van and a tent. Rangers were personable and helpful. Bathrooms clean and stocked. Be aware that only certain loops have a bear box in each campsite. Hiking, weather, and views were terrific.

reviews.author: Katie M.
reviews.text: This campground is beautiful!  The rangers and the camp host were so polite and personable.  We stayed in loop C and this loop has a very tight turn at the end of it and we barely fit.  The trees had damage so other people have definitely hit them multiple times.  Our site was C28, a very long pull through.  We have a 30 foot trailer with a 20 foot tow vehicle.  We could not pull through this site due to a tree, but we were able to back in the trailer with ease.  Any longer than us would probably not be able to successfully drive through the loop.  Out site was huge and quite far away from other campers.  The kids loved how much room there was to play under the trees.  This is a very wooded campground and it was wonderful to relax under the trees.  This campground is within walking distance of the Carter Falls trailhead, I highly recommend this hike as well as this campground!

reviews.author: Danielle G.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite, peaceful and had just what we needed

reviews.author: Wei G.
reviews.text: 营地非常有人气，工作人员也非常热情！下次还想去！

reviews.author: Shaunna B.
reviews.text: Just a very relaxing experience. Restrooms were clean, and the campground was quiet. Mt. Rainier as a whole is a life event you’ll never forget!

reviews.author: Stephen P.
reviews.text: Dump station is closed and its very inconvenient since the road through the park to other campgrounds is closed.   Campers need better access to drinking water.   Also, site C12 is used as a cut through to the bathrooms from Loop B because there is no trail around.  It was not great having people constantly walk though our campsite while we were trying to have a campfire or cook dinner.

reviews.author: Ben J.
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful camp grounds in one of the most beautiful places. We booked one night but the next 2 nights were booked out but the recreation.gov staff booked us another site for those next two nights so we were able to stay the whole time we needed which was fantastic. Unforgettable experience and stay.

reviews.author: Cheryl F.
reviews.text:
Enjoyed camping here! Mt Rainier was massive and covered in snow, a sight to behold! 
Our CG site was very spacious, and we were close to many great hiking trails. I was a little disappointed because a large number of trees had been taken down in the campground due to disease.

reviews.author: Mike C.
reviews.text:
Beautiful sites. 
We stayed here for a night before climbing Rainier the next day and found our site super clean and quiet and welcoming. Friendly staff and great facilities.

reviews.author: Shauna  Y.
reviews.text:
Had no problem getting our 30ft RV into loop E. Stayed at site 25.
Spots are relatively close together, not much privacy. Still, a beautiful location and you can see Mt. Rainier peeking through the trees. 
We had three teenagers and a dog and everyone was very happy! We’d totally stay here again.

reviews.author: Carol P.
reviews.text: Beautiful place.  The bathrooms were clean.

reviews.author: Isabelle  B.
reviews.text: Camping is nice with plenty of trees and nature so you are a bit private on your site. Restrooms are OK. We would have liked to be able to buy woods directly at the camground instead of going to another place.

reviews.author: Min Z.
reviews.text: Very friendly staff, clean camp space and bathrooms. Note that there is no hot water and the tap water is very cold.

reviews.author: Brody B.
reviews.text: Grandson and I had a great experience.  Beautiful campground and was perfect for my truck tent.  Restrooms and water areas clean and not too far to walk to.

reviews.author: Linda C.
reviews.text: Wonderful campsite with privacy.

reviews.author: William M.
reviews.text: Cozy campground. Toilets were nice - our space was a bit crooked, but otherwise nice and spacious.

reviews.author: Anna B.
reviews.text: We stayed in Loop B, site 35 a pull through site. The entrance is shared with the site next to it, but we were not close!  A large rig would have difficulty pulling through, but ours was right at 27’. Pull thru pad has a slight slope to the right side. Large campsite and even though the road is on the other side of the site, the noise is almost non-exsistent. We would definitely pick this site again.

reviews.author: Amy C.
reviews.text: really hard to tell where the restrooms are per loop and how to get to them

reviews.author: Doris M.
reviews.text: Lovely campsite. We were in Loop C really close to the restroom but still had very decent privacy. Very close to Longmire Museum and Henry Jackson Visitor Center. The site was generally quiet but sometimes, even after quiet hours, group laughter can be heard from a few sites away, though it didn't really bother us because we were exhausted from our day's adventures. The bear box was a great commodity to stash our food away so we didn't have to worry about our food. Restrooms were well-kept and stocked with toilet paper and paper towel. The water is cold though so bring facial wipes if you don't like washing your face with cold water. The ranger volunteers were very friendly and gave us a couple recommendations. They walk around the campsite to check on things but didn't bother anyone unless they needed to. We would stay again!

reviews.author: JULIE P.
reviews.text: Great basecamp for a visit to Mt Rainier--easy access to Longmire and Paradise and mayn trailheads. Campsites on A Loop are quite close together. Look for sites with more space and foliage in between on other loops.

reviews.author: Gregory K.
reviews.text: Mount Rainier is a wonderful place to visit.  Lots of hikes and beautiful scenery.  Unfortunately, when anything needs repair, it is a long time coming.  The RV dump station at Cougar Rock Campground is on its 2nd year of being nonoperational. There were no operational comfort stations (rest/washrooms) in loop B. The path from Loop B to the Loop C comfort station is blocked by downfall and you have to encroach into someone else's campsite to go to the bathroom.  Park Rangers, get these things fixed!

reviews.author: James S.
reviews.text: Trees and forest was beautiful. Although we had no reservations, the ranger was very helpful and accommodating. Clean park, clean restrooms. Highly recommend this campground.

reviews.author: Ursula M.
reviews.text: Nice place to Star and visit mt Rainier!!

reviews.author: Tyler B.
reviews.text: Camp sites close together. Clean bathrooms, great views, friendly people. I would stay again but choose site carefully.

reviews.author: Lindsay M.
reviews.text: nice large campground. bathrooms had soap. water bottle fill station is delicious.

reviews.author: Mert K.
reviews.text: Narada falls is a great hiking spot without having to drive anywhere from the campsite! Pretty light trail with tons of width for multiple groups at a time.

reviews.author: Dennis V.
reviews.text:
Clean restroom, tent sites large enough.
Friendly knowledgeable rangers

reviews.author: Denis B.
reviews.text: As far as designated, maintained campgrounds where you are relatively close to other people, this is one of the best. There are a lot of trees and vegetation that provide privacy. There are bathrooms and fresh water. The campground is beautiful and close to other park attractions. The Rampart Ridge and Wonderland Trails are only a few minutes away.

reviews.author: Camille S.
reviews.text: Overall a good experience, I appreciated the staff at check-in -- it was nice and convenient to have actual employees present at the site, who knew the campground well. While the restroom facilities were very clean and the site itself fine, I was very concerned about the quantity of standing dead trees in the campground -- not just a few, but dozens of standing dead trees, poised above restrooms, campsites, parking areas etc. Some had been marked with paint, but the sites were not closed. I hope that in the future, NPS at this site will take their hazard tree program more seriously.

reviews.author: Scarlett L.
reviews.text: Best location!

reviews.author: Carol P.
reviews.text: Nice campsite, clean restrooms, helpful Park Ranger, a nice trail, and not too far from the Park's amenities.

reviews.author: Hope P.
reviews.text: This was a lovely campsite. I thought being front country it would be louder or more crowded, but it wasn't. The campsites were nicely spaced and there was a nice spot for the tent. There were many trees and the bathrooms were clean.

reviews.author: Delara G.
reviews.text: Great campground with caring host & managers!

reviews.author: Jonathon T.
reviews.text: Nice, quiet forested campground.  Clean restroom.  Great location on The Mountain.

reviews.author: Richard  B.
reviews.text: Always a great place to stay! but I don't know why they only have one Loop open in the middle of September

reviews.author: Laura A.
reviews.text: The campsite was great, lots of trees and just enough space for our tent.

reviews.author: Caroline W.
reviews.text: Cougar Rick Campground is perfect for seeing the sights and getting to trailheads near Paradise.

reviews.author: Grace D.
reviews.text: This site had a great tent pad. It was very woodsy and peaceful all around. Good bathrooms. Beautiful national park as well!

reviews.author: JULIE F.
reviews.text: Great park - just wished it wasn't foggy the two days we were there......Camp spot and bathrooms were awesome!

reviews.author: Darin G.
reviews.text: A fine campground, especially if you want to spend time at Longmire or Paradise. The walk to Longmire, on the Wonderland Trail, is pleasant and easy, about a mile and a half and 500 feet down.  Many good trails out of Longmire if you feel like a longer hike from there.  From Cougar Rock you can also walk the Wonderland to Reflection Lakes or even Paradise, but it's longer with much more elevation gain than the Longmire hike.

reviews.author: Erik G.
reviews.text: Campsite was not even close to a good area. Half on top of a small cliff, with the tent site barely fitting at the bottom of a 15 foot drop down. This shouldn't have been a camping spot.

reviews.author: Dodo B.
reviews.text: Well marshaled campground.  Close to some great hiking trails.

reviews.author: Robert R.
reviews.text: Good tent surface

reviews.author: Leslie G.
reviews.text: We pulled in on the Friday morning after Labor Day and, since it was first come first served, were directed to check in with a ranger, who assigned us to a campsite, which was very helpful so that we didn't end up going around loops looking. Turns out several of the campground loops were closed so it ended up being a very quiet and peaceful experience. I appreciated the ample space in the campsite and between campsites as well.

reviews.author: Tatum L.
reviews.text: Private, quiet and clean campgroup within walking or short driving distance to all the hikes we wanted to do.

reviews.author: Jeroldine H.
reviews.text: Great campground, lots of privacy, restrooms well-maintained. Our main concern was the lack of clarity /communication online about the gradual shut-down of most of the loops. The only ones open were C loop and Roadside sites. Of five open sites, we had to choose one, site-unseen, despite arriving early in the day. We wish the entire campground were open through September. This is a very popular time to visit.

reviews.author: Nelson K.
