reviews.text: Camping site is spacious, quiet. Bath room is clean. It easy to access the trail.

reviews.author: David H.
reviews.text: Conveniently located with NP. Beautiful forest and large trees provided much shade (not always a good thing when you want your solar batteries to charge!  Sites were large and mostly level.  Good cell service. Facilities were clean and well maintained. We loved our stay in Mt Ranier!

reviews.author: Chris M.
reviews.text: Great Campground with access to tens of hiking trails in the park.

reviews.author: Deborah c.
reviews.text:
Beautiful setting. Nice camp spots.
Though in need of a lot of maintenance, many parts of the campground were closed due to dangerous trees.

reviews.author: Nancy L.
reviews.text: Good Location in the park.  Restroom very clean.  Some locations cannot get water

reviews.author: Karin K.
reviews.text: A beautiful campground with lovely, private sites among a towering forest. I camped solo and felt perfectly safe. Nice access to bathrooms and very tasty running water that one seems to only find in the mountains. Also - flush toilets, which is quite the luxury at a campground. I enjoyed every moment of my stay and only wished it was longer. I'll be back!

reviews.author: Stephanie M.
reviews.text:
Many, including entire loops, of campsites continue to be closed since last year due to "tree hazards".  Also, it was extremely inconvenient that the RV dump station was closed. We had to drive out of our way to find an alternative to dump our gray/black water. Why was the dump station closed prior to Labor Day Weekend? Finally, my family and I were very disappointed that there were no interpretive presentations with the rangers. We have visited Cougar Rock for several years and also look forward to this fun, educational program. 

Are all these issues due to a lack of federal funding? If so, I hope it changes.

reviews.author: Nelson K.
reviews.text: Restroom is clean, site is spacious and quite

reviews.author: Matt M.
reviews.text: Great campground with beautiful sites. Good amount of space and vegetation between sites. Located close to paradise for easy access.

reviews.author: Jack H.
reviews.text: I enjoyed Cougar Rock campground and Mt Rainier National Park. The location of the campground was excellent for going to the Paradise trails and the nearby trail to Carter Falls was an excellent hike. I enjoyed seeing all of the wildflowers on the Paradise trails, even in late august.

reviews.author: Carl Y.
reviews.text: We have camped regularly at Cougar Rock campground almost since it opened half a century ago. And, I have to say, this campground is pretty beat up and in desperate need of renovation. Not counting the fact that at least one-third of the sites are uninhabitable because of “Hazard Trees.” All of the sites need to be rethought and reworked; rocks and trees are under tables; fire pits are too near dying firs; the ADA-toilet program has more than fifty sites using one male and two female toilets; asphalt is crumbling at the edge of parking pads. NPS, you can do better.

reviews.author: Andrew N.
reviews.text: Wish they had electricity at sites.  Phone signal was also a problem - none. Campground was too primitive for a five star rating, but running water in bathrooms was nice. Also many sites were closed because of hazard trees — campground needs some serious maintenance and upgrades to become the excellent type of campground that a national park deserves.

reviews.author: Pakou L.
reviews.text: My boyfriend and I did a walk in for the cougar campsite at Mt. Rainer. We arrived early so we were able to take the 4th to last walk in campsite. We loved our spot and enjoyed our stay. All the campsites on Cougar Rock are a little close to each other, so if you want privacy, this may not be your best choice, however, I didn't mind it. I definitely recommend  Cougar. I felt it was close to other trails and loved it was near the Nisqually River Walkway.

reviews.author: Judith Z.
reviews.text:
It's a great campground and within a short drive to Paradise and excellent hiking on Mt. Rainier.  sorry we were to late for
all the wild flowers.  We usually come a couple of weeks earlier.

reviews.author: Neal A.
reviews.text: The assignment site was extremely uneven and no amount of blocking was going to solve that issue. Also, the space was so small and enclosed by tree branches it was hard to open the door.

reviews.author: Jarred H.
reviews.text: Excellent Campground. Perfect location for everything great about Mt Rainier in the Paradise area. Hosts were nice and accommodating.

reviews.author: Sue M.
reviews.text: A memorable trip to a remarkable park and campground. Although our site had some leveling issues, we were able to resolve them and spend two wonderful days at Mount Ranier. Cool weather made for comfortable hiking and the Longmire and other park Visitor’s centers provided all the information that we needed for a great visit. Despite COVID restrictions, park staff throughout the park were very supportive and helpful with their recommendations and the information they provided.

reviews.author: Kyle R.
reviews.text: Good campsite with amenities near paradise part of park

reviews.author: Rob B.
reviews.text: Nice campground.  Big trees, quiet.  Site next to us had a generator running  a couple hours per day.  Also bathrooms had big lights which did shine in our site.

reviews.author: Barbara H.
reviews.text: The sites were very close but in a lovely wooded setting.

reviews.author: Tim C.
reviews.text: With no notice prior to our arrival, our site was switched due to safety reasons to another site that was totally inappropriate for the length of our RV and would have been impossible to level.  This same site situation happened to the party we were traveling with and they wound up in a loop furthest away from our relocated site.  On site park personnel were of no assistance and uncooperative because there were other suitable sites we found that were not reserved or occupied but the park representative said they were not available.  Also, the dump station at this campground was shut down.  We had no alternative but to find other campsites at a national forest campground some distance outside of the national park.  Cougar Rock campground in My Rainier National Park is a poorly maintained facility manned by a poorly trained staff.

reviews.author: Dick C.
reviews.text: We try to get up to Rainier at least once a year and we like staying at the Cougar Rock campground.  The campground itself is well maintained - a variety of good sites, clean restrooms, etc. - and it is conveniently located on the Wonderland Trail.  A nice easy hike along the Nisqually takes you down river to Longmire or you can hike in the other direction toward Paradise.  It is also far enough up the mountain that you can drive to Paradise from your campsite early in the morning and beat the crowds - hike the trails around Paradise amidst the wild flowers and then head back to your campsite for lunch.  It's my favorite place and has been since my first visit in 1949 when I was 6 years old.

reviews.author: Ken B.
reviews.text: Campsite was fine, bathrooms were clean.  Checkin was easy.  Bear box was operable and empty when I got there.  White River has better bottle fillers.

reviews.author: Cassandra L.
reviews.text: We really like the group site - enough space for privacy but also feel intimate and easy to connect with your friends and family. The location is very close to the Paradise, easy access to Wonderland Trail.

reviews.author: Celeste O.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Most sites are very good although many were closed due to tree hazards. I’m hoping they can get the sites functioning again as the campground stays booked on their sites. If you are not able to camp after booking a reservation please make sure to cancel it so others can use the camp site.

reviews.author: Grace T.
reviews.text: We had a great experience at cougar rock campground. The campsite was private, and the location was excellent. Hiking the High Skyline Trail at Paradise was one of our most memorable activities of the trip.

reviews.author: Linda S.
reviews.text:
Rangers were welcoming and very helpful.
Bathrooms were clean! Campsite was a little small but very nice.

reviews.author: Richard B.
reviews.text: The campground is in serious need of repair.  Many of the sites are closed.  Streets have pot holes, pull throughs are not level.  I have been camping at Cougar Rock for more than 50 years, and a total of 60 years at Mt. Rainier.  I first was camping with my family at the Longmire campground and then when Cougar Rock was new we started camping up there.  Obviously the park is underfunded.  I would  double, or triple fees and start putting money back into the campground and have park rangers available.  The other thing you could do is send emails like Yellowstone does and requests gifts towards specific projects.  I would easily donate if I knew where my funds were going, ie. trails, camping sites, restoration etc.

reviews.author: Sally V.
reviews.text: x

reviews.author: Jennifer M.
reviews.text: I was shocked that there was NO water spigot in loop B. Also no bathroom, which makes very lite sense, but no water makes NO sense.

reviews.author: Thomas D.
reviews.text: The condition of the park is deteriorating but we had a great time there it's too bad they don't clean it up and open up the other loop it could use some pavement work and tree clean up. We would like to see our tax dollars at work.

reviews.author: Jenna B.
reviews.text: Perfect place to stay in the park!

reviews.author: Sue C.
reviews.text:
We always love our stays at Cougar Rock Campground.  The sites are nice and big albeit not all that level or flat. They are manageable. 
It was very uncrowded due to the closure of so many camp sites for downed trees and closure of A Loop entirely. It was a quiet and restful trip to the mountain!
We hiked up around Paradise which was beautiful and warm this year.  The smoke from wildfires came the next day and held the temps at bay. The Nisqually River as running high and fast because of the heat and glacial melt.  Amazing crossing at the log bridge!

reviews.author: Harvey Z.
reviews.text: Camped here in a beautiful location. I could see Mt. Rainier from the campground.

reviews.author: Danielle N.
reviews.text: What a great campground! We really enjoyed being within the park! Our sites were great, we had C005 and C007. We really couldn't have asked for a better weekend getaway!

reviews.author: Keith D.
reviews.text: Very quiet and nice campground.  Clean bathrooms.  Close to Paradise Lodge and many great day hikes.  Will be back.

reviews.author: Natalie B.
reviews.text: The rangers were helpful. The camp sites had a picnic table and a bear box. There were shared bathrooms with plumbing and water. No cell phone service but I really enjoyed not having phone service and my time there. Close to Paradise and the trails there.

reviews.author: Mike T.
reviews.text: Bring a small tent, there isn't much level space available on the sites.

reviews.author: Kevin N.
reviews.text: Camping was awesome.  There were a few problems with the bathrooms.  We had to walk a bit to the next few loops.

reviews.author: Alexa W.
reviews.text: Walk-in sites were luckily available. Potable water, clean site, bathroom with TP, food storage bins.

reviews.author: sangmok k.
reviews.text: We've been there last week and It was the best place to go to the Mt Rainier National park.

reviews.author: Xuan L.
reviews.text: Great place. Close to Paradise. Bathroom is clean. Ranger program at night was super fun and educational.

reviews.author: Gretchen K.
reviews.text: Campground was very clean and well organized.  The host was very informative and eager to answer our questions.  Like most of our national parks, Mt Rainier was very crowded.  I am concerned about the crowds damaging the environment and would encourage NPS to limit the number of visitors.

reviews.author: Jonathan C.
reviews.text: Convenient location for thru-hiking, hot showers would be nice.

reviews.author: Mike T.
reviews.text: Small sites but a neat little Campground with clean restrooms and good tasting water.

reviews.author: Lynda F.
reviews.text: x

reviews.author: Michael R.
reviews.text:
Great campground.  Make sure you obey the size limitation. We have a 31' RV and some corners were tight around the campground.
Dump Station was close which was a a bummer.
Great Location and very nice sites.

reviews.author: Steven V.
reviews.text: Hosts were very hospitable.

reviews.author: Claudia D.
reviews.text:
Beautiful campground location in the heart of Mount Rainier.  
We loved the Ranger presentation at the Cougar Rock amphitheater Saturday night!
Well-maintained campground. Location, location, location — minutes from Longmire and Paradise and easy access to many trails, including Wonderland. 
This is a favorite destination for our group.

reviews.author: Don R.
reviews.text: Other than the dump station being closed, and no activity for the amphitheater,  we enjoyed seeing our grandkids experience Mt Rainier and Cougar Rock.  I remember when the park rangers use to speak to the campers/kids or tell stories every night during the summer.  Miss those days and wish my grandkids could experience that.

reviews.author: Katie Q.
reviews.text: Great views, clean facilities and quiet campground! Would go back!

reviews.author: Cory L.
reviews.text: Very clean and quiet campground. Highly recommend to stay here if you're visiting Paradise. Campground hosts were very friendly and helpful. We enjoyed having the park ranger programs back!

reviews.author: Peter F.
reviews.text: Awesome spot for a morning hike on Mt. Rainier

reviews.author: John J.
reviews.text: Hazard tree had us moved to B13 instead of the B25 we had originally reserved. B13 appeared to be the inly site in the B loop with absolute zero shade during the hottest hours of the day between about 10:30am to 5pm during the summer months (we were there for Sunday-Saturday last week of July). We were in the backcountry on a 20 mile hike with a total of about 6000ft elevation gain for one of the nights and just wanted to rest the following day, but could not because it was just unbearably hot without a spot of shade. Avoid B13 like the plague, unless you bring your own means to create shade (pop-up canopy with walls), or are certain you will be out and about during the hot hours.

reviews.author: Tarun A.
reviews.text: One of our best camping experience ever!! Bathroom was super clean.

reviews.author: Joseph C.
reviews.text: Tightly packed campsites with multiple downed/hazardous trees minimizing available sites. Our restroom was closed so we had to walk to adjacent loop. Generator hours were a mystery until we found them on the back of White River camping brochure.

reviews.author: Heena R.
reviews.text: The Best Campground to stay inside the National Park and visit/hike the places on Paradise, Longmire side. We stayed here for 3 days and did back-to-back hikes of  Skyline Trail, Camp Muir. Spend one day of sightseeing and doing small easy hikes of  Nisqually Vista trail, Narada falls (lower viewpoint), Reflection lake, Drive Steven Canyon.  Glad we got this opportunity to stay at Cougar Campground. Previous year we had a reservation but had to cancel our trip as our camping tent site was under hazardous trees.  This time got to see what the site of a hazardous tree looks like.  The Rangers are doing an amazing job of keeping the Campground maintained.

reviews.author: Liv M.
reviews.text: I believe half of the sites at Cougar Rock are "first come first serve".  This was very helpful for us because even though we arrived before noon on a Wednesday we got the last campsite but it was only available for one night and we wanted two.  We got in line before 7:30 the next morning for a "first come first serve" site and just got one.  We cold have stayed longer with this site but didn't need to.  It was lovely to walk by the rushing river and around Christine Falls and the beautiful Nadara Falls both very close. The rangers were wonderful.

reviews.author: Pam T.
reviews.text: Ranger was very helpful.  I liked their system of labeling the sites availability for first come first served

reviews.author: Brian S.
reviews.text: Great spot to explore the mountain

reviews.author: Karen G.
reviews.text: Much of campground is closed due to tree hazards. Many first come first served sites available daily IF you get to campground ranger station at 7:30 am. Do NOT drive campground to pick your own site- they will assign you one based on availability and your equipment. Super convenient for Paradise side of Mt. Rainier.

reviews.author: Joy R.
reviews.text: What a beautiful camp ground! Lovely sites, clean bathrooms, and friendly neighbors.  Couldn’t ask for more perfection!  Oh and the rangers were very helpful!

reviews.author: Donna B.
reviews.text: Great campground. Lots of maintenance issues, hazard trees, septic, water. At least at 2/3 capacity due to one closed loop and closed sites.

reviews.author: Duane M.
reviews.text: Very friendly and helpful. Staff was pleasant and very eager to answer questions

reviews.author: Anne W.
reviews.text: The campsite we reserved had been closed due to dangerous trees but we were not notified in advance to our arrival of the change.  Either the site was not tagged upon our arrival, or we did not notice the sign, or the sign was posted after we set up camp, either way, we did set up camp and a park ranger even drove by and waived at us as we were sitting around the camp fire.  At 6:00 am the following morning, we were awoken by a loud female voice yelling at us that we had to move to a different location.  It was one of the camp hosts and she told us to check with the ranger station to find out where we were supposed to move to.  From that point on, we were harassed by the camp hosts at our new location.  Training should be provided to your camp hosts to include harassment.  This was my second camping trip to Mt Rainier and it will be my last because of our experience at Cougar Rock.

reviews.author: Zachary B.
reviews.text: Perfect Campsite

reviews.author: Marc B.
reviews.text: Great place and a lot of fun.

reviews.author: Robbie S.
reviews.text: Stayed at Cougar Rock on non-consecutive nights last week. We were in Loop D and took the short walk to the Wonderland Trail by the Nisqually River. Found a quiet, secluded place to watch the sunset on Rainier - it was breath-taking! One of our favorite campsites from our trip.

reviews.author: Anna C.
reviews.text: Great place to stay. Loved the easy walk to the reservoir to cool off.

reviews.author: Mike G.
reviews.text: Clean campground with great sites!  Great location as well!

reviews.author: Takeshi N.
reviews.text:
Good campsite. 
Not too far to visitor center.

reviews.author: Linda F.
reviews.text:
Very quiet campground. Lovely setting.
The area has wonderful opportunities for hiking and is a great location between Longmire and Paradise.

reviews.author: Isabel T.
reviews.text: Great location in Mt Rainier NP. Clean bathrooms (with open door, which made me more comfortable sharing sinks, etc. with maskless strangers). Our campsite in the B loop was surrounded by cut-down trees, so it was slightly smaller than expected and not the most visually appealing.

reviews.author: Jennifer  P.
reviews.text: Great campground in Mt. Rainier. It was rainy when we arrived but we made the best of it and hiked Carter Falls across the way in the rain. We had the trail all to ourselves!

reviews.author: Gayle M.
reviews.text: Campsites are nestled in amongst the trees so they feel somewhat private. Hiking trails are close by. The bathrooms had soap this year! Appreciate how quiet the campground was at night.

reviews.author: Fiona S.
reviews.text: The campground was fantastic. Large but we still felt like there was privacy. The walks are amazing, including one from right near the campground.

reviews.author: Tonya Y.
reviews.text: This review is for site R014, which we got by first-come first-serve the day after we spent the night at a reserved site on this campground. We thought there'd be no way we could get one on a holiday weekend in the summer, but the camp host told us if we came by 6 or 6:30am the next day, we would definitely be able to get a spot. This was true, as there were only 3 parties in line for a spot by the time the park ranger came at 7:30 to let us sign up. This spot is nearly right across the road from the bathroom (but not too close to be bothersome) which was very convenient, and the tent pad has ample space. Parking is in a combined area with the neighboring site. I'm only giving this 4 stars because there was no food locker.

reviews.author: Tonya Y.
reviews.text: This review is for site B027. The stated tent pad dimensions are 5'x7', which sounded quite small... I brought an additional small backpacking tent just in case we needed it, but we ended up being able to pitch our 7'x9' tent with the exception of one of the vestibules! We were butted right up against a small rock lodged in the ground, but otherwise it was much better than expected. This site does have a fire pit and food locker, even though the pictures don't show them.

reviews.author: Stephen B.
reviews.text: Camp ground host was great. Very professional, courteous and knowledgeable. Quite a few sites were not available due to dangerous tree conditions but the campground was beautiful. Bring your own firewood. Nothing available

reviews.author: Rika H.
reviews.text: Nice and quiet camp ground.   Friendly rangers and camp host.  The trail to Carter Falls is closed due to bridge got washed away during the heat wave..

reviews.author: Alison L.
reviews.text: Tidy facilities. Note that sites are pretty close together.

reviews.author: Rob G.
reviews.text: Mount Rainier National Park and Cougar Rock Campground are the best.  Many hikes for all capabilities close by.  The campground is beautiful forest, respectful people, quiet, and friendly.

reviews.author: Laren N.
reviews.text: The gentlemen who help me the day of Check-in provided superior customer service.

reviews.author: Jue H.
reviews.text: Great campground. Each site is spacious  With fire pit and table. Bathroom has flush toilet and is clean. The campground is well maintained. Most of ppl there were quiet except some car alarm went off early morning which woke up most of ppl.

reviews.author: Erik W.
reviews.text: Great hiking and falls. Although reservations  were booked up, I was able to get a first come first serve site. If you do this get there early as they go fast!

reviews.author: Andrew S.
reviews.text: Great campsites in the amazing Mt. Rainier National Park! It was the first overnight camp for my son, and he loved every minute.

reviews.author: Victor G.
reviews.text: Our site was perfect, but perfect depends on your neighbor here. Good or bad? That depends on you and where your nearest human being is. Treat each other well and all shall mostly be good. Happy camping.

reviews.author: Christopher B.
reviews.text: I liked that the campground was in a good location for exploring the south side of the park. Considering the location, I felt the campsites were nicely spaced.

reviews.author: Joshua S.
reviews.text: Wonderful campsite; accommodate our request for quiet and secluded, shady site. Clean.

reviews.author: Linh D.
reviews.text:
Secluded with lots of trees and shade, quiet, & clean.
Near lots of hiking trails, waterfalls, streams, and creeks.

reviews.author: Ritajane B.
reviews.text:
There are no dump stations in Mt. Rainier National Park.  That is a great inconvenience for us since we are older with some disabilities.  To stay in the park the 4 nights reserved, we had to make a 30 mile round trip with our trailer outside the park to find a dump station.  The ranger said they had not been available for two years.  Is there a reason you are not fixing the dump stations?  

Much deferred maintenance.  Many campsites closed and loop A closed due to tree hazards.  Much work needs to be done to clear the camp and completely open it.  However, our campsite was nice.

reviews.author: Melissa M.
reviews.text:
Cougar Rock Campground is beautiful!   We took our 2 kids (9 and 11) and 18' travel trailer to camp there and as the descriptions say it can get pretty tight in there- rocks and trees right alongside the roadways.  The bathrooms were clean and well stocked.  We also appreciated the  water spigots right outside of the bath house.  There was a little room with an odd looking sink (think utility-tub meets toilet, meets bidet...) for waste water from dishes, etc. in the bath house.

We really enjoyed that just across the street from the campground was the best place to view Mt. Rainier in our experience.  Its along the river and is one of many places that you can hop onto the Wonderland Trail.  One evening we took our bag chairs and relaxed next to the river overlooking Mt. Rainier. 

We also got on the Wonderland Trail and headed for Longmire where we hiked the Trail of the Shadows.  It was a pretty hike, just be prepared for a lot of trees.  That stretch of the Wonderland Trail is also very pretty and not terribly difficult.  There are bathrooms and a general store in Longmire.

We went up to the Henry M. Jackson V.C. and the ranger there was FANTASTIC!  That part of the park was still under snow and being from Michigan we didn't stick around (we've had our fill...)  ;)  I was bumming that we wouldn't get to see the wildflowers, but even in the end of June they just weren't ready yet.  Our kids did the Junior Ranger program and they have new books that were engaging and fun to do.  *If you are not sure that you'll be able to get back to a Visitor Center by the end of your trip, tell the ranger when you pick up the book and they will usually let you take the badge with you on the condition that you promise to have the kids take the pledge before you hand over the badge.

reviews.author: Daniel F.
reviews.text: Complete chaos in the booking system. I made the reservation early in the year. Recreation.gov said the site I selected for Thursday night was a first-come first-serve campsite on Friday and Saturday. However, this information proved inaccurate because when we called about a week before to check the reservation, we were told it was not a first-come first-serve site after all. This is not what the website stated when I made my initial reservation. Because of this error, I had to get in line at 6:30am and wait 90 minutes to secure another campsite. Then we had to pack up our campsite by noon and wait until 2pm for another camper to vacate our new campsite. We spent the whole morning waiting around instead of going out and seeing the park. And then the other camper did not vacate the new campsite that we rented - his camper remained parked at the campsite all afternoon. We finally just set up our tent around 3pm. The other camper did not return until almost 5pm and claimed that he also had a reservation for the same campsite - he showed us a receipt and said "I'm not leaving." Because of the disorganized and chaotic booking process we wasted the whole day and ended up having to share the campsite with a stranger.

reviews.text:
We love camping for a week each August at Cougar Rock Campground and have done so since the kids were in diapers.  It's very important to reserve a campsite as soon as possible for that popular time of year! Of the three main campgrounds in Mt. Rainier National Park, Cougar Rock is the closest to Paradise (yet still 20-30 minutes away), a number of trailheads, right off the famed round-the-mountain Wonderland Trail, and only a couple miles by road or easy trail from Longmire where you can restock, buy souvenirs, and lodge.  Immediate must-see destination from the campground is an easy 100-yard walk along the road and down the bank to the Nisqually River, with a view of Mt. Rainier.  At this point, the river is well confined but the riverbed is wide; walk the trail, it's the Wonderland Trail in fact, across the riverbed and log bridge over the Nisqually River for pics.

Drive early in the day to Paradise, as it's crowded even during the week. Visit the new-ish visitor center, see the exhibits and pick up a map of the many trails around the Paradise area.  Glacier Vista, Alta Vista, and the Skyline Trail are three short to long famous ones. Link for Skyline Trail here, or use the WTA.ORG site. https://www.outdoorproject.com/united-states/washington/skyline-trail-hike On your way to Paradise, stop at Christine Falls, Narada Falls, or the big pull out vista a mile or more after you cross the Nisqually River. If Paradise is too crowded for you, visit Reflection Lakes (best reflection times early and late in the day, sorry!), and hike to the Pinnacle-Plummer Saddle or do the Lakes Trail Loop, also accessible from Paradise, which can make for a nice connecting hike if you have a couple of cars.

reviews.author: Teri G.
reviews.text: Weather withstanding, our time at Cougar Rock Campground was amazing.  We did have the biggest thunderstorm of the decade roll through right on top of us, but that just made it more exciting.  The sites are what you would expect from a National Park campground:  you can see and hear your neighbors, but lights out at 10pm, so sleeping is not a problem. The sites are pretty flat, and most have plenty of room for a tent and covered kitchen set up.  Bring a canopy with walls, not just screens, as there could be rain. The camp is situated in an old grove forest and lower in elevation, which means you wont be so cold.  This is Washington and the insect population changes as the temperature does.  We camped in August, but because of the cooler temps, we had no mosquitoes. Bug repellent in August is probably recommended.  The ranger station is located at the entrance to the campground, with wood for sale from the camphost, and information at the ranger station when open.  Weather for the day is displayed.

reviews.author: Mark P.
reviews.text: We never “visited” the campground because our reservation (made 6 months in advance) was canceled while we were on our 9 week cross-country trip. Thankful I got the email cancellation while we were in Canada. The email said WE had requested the cancellation. NOT!!!  They were doing some tree trimming. Very poor customer relations!!

reviews.author: Justin M.
reviews.text: Love it.

reviews.author: Raden S.
reviews.text: My wife and I stayed here one night on a driving tour of Washington. There was a ranger-lead activity that we did not attend but had gotten favorable reviews from neighbor kids. The campsite was well maintained; the bathrooms were very clean; water was readily available; firewood was also readily available.

reviews.author: Carl H.
reviews.text: It is a beautiful campground with large a space for the RV. Bathroom facilities were very clean. The best feature at Cougar Rock was its location to most major sites within the park.
